title: Spotify Introduces Running Mode Feature
content:
Spotify Unveils Running Mode to Enhance Fitness Workouts

In a bid to revolutionize the way users create playlists for their workouts, music streaming giant Spotify has introduced a new feature called Running Mode. This innovative tool aims to simplify the process of finding the perfect music to match an individual's fitness goals, musical preferences, and desired beats per minute (BPM). According to Spotify, Running Mode is designed to save users time and effort, allowing them to focus on their workouts rather than searching for the right music.

The Running Mode feature utilizes AI technology to provide a personalized experience, building on the capabilities introduced with Prompted Playlists last year. Spotify has observed that fitness-based prompts have proven to be extremely popular among users, and this new feature caters to that demand. Running Mode offers customizable running presets and optional coaching features, making it an attractive addition to the Spotify Premium subscription.

To access the Running Mode feature, users will need a Premium subscription to Spotify. With this new tool, fitness enthusiasts can expect to find the perfect blend of music and motivation to enhance their workouts. As Spotify continues to evolve and adapt to user needs, Running Mode represents a significant step forward in the company's commitment to providing a seamless and engaging music experience.
author: The Verge

title: Spotify introduces Running Mode for iOS Premium users
content:
Apple has announced that its new Running Mode feature will soon be available to Premium subscribers on iOS devices, but only in a limited number of countries. The update is part of the company’s ongoing effort to enhance its fitness ecosystem for users who have opted into the paid tier of its health and activity services.

Running Mode is designed to provide real‑time coaching, route optimization and performance metrics tailored for runners. The feature will be rolled out to Premium users on iOS in select markets, with availability dates and country lists to be confirmed in the coming weeks. Users who are not in the eligible regions will not see the option until the feature expands globally. The company has stated that the rollout will begin with a pilot program to ensure stability and performance before a wider release.
author: TechCrunch

title: German Chancellor's Holiday Reading Choice
content:
Friedrich Merz, the German politician whose popularity has slipped to record lows, has turned to a different form of respite this summer. In a move that has attracted media attention, the former CDU leader is reportedly packing the papal guide *Magifica Humanitas* for a live European tour, a departure from the typical beach reads that dominate the season. The guide, a collection of spiritual essays and reflections, is said to accompany Merz as he seeks guidance amid the political turbulence that has marked his brief tenure in office.

The decision to bring a religious text on a public tour underscores the broader context of Merz’s recent challenges. Since taking office 14 months ago, he has faced a series of controversies and policy setbacks that have eroded public confidence. By choosing a spiritually oriented reading list, Merz appears to be looking for moral and personal clarity while also projecting an image of calm and reflection. The tour, which will include stops across key European capitals, is expected to provide a platform for the former party leader to address his supporters and the wider electorate.

While the initiative may signal a desire to reconnect with constituents, observers note that the effectiveness of such a gesture remains uncertain. The timing of the tour, coinciding with the summer’s traditional leisure period, could be interpreted as an attempt to shift focus from political criticism to personal renewal. Whether the papal guide will resonate with voters or simply serve as a symbolic act will likely unfold over the coming weeks as Merz continues to navigate the challenges of his leadership role.
author: Guardian Technology

title: UK Authorities Seize Assets in Crackdown on Spam Texts
content:
The UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) carried out a series of search warrants on Wednesday, seizing laptops, mobile phones and documents from residences and offices linked to five companies operating in London, Liverpool, Bolton, Burnley and Swansea. The action follows a growing investigation into a car‑finance mis‑selling scandal in which consumers reportedly received spam text messages advertising finance deals that were later found to be misleading or unsuitable.

The warrants were part of a broader crackdown on the companies’ marketing practices, which the ICO alleges involved the distribution of unsolicited messages that encouraged customers to sign up for finance agreements without fully disclosing the terms or risks. By targeting the firms’ communications infrastructure and record‑keeping systems, the ICO aims to gather evidence of potential breaches of the Data Protection Act and the Consumer Credit Act.

The seizure of electronic devices and documents is expected to provide the ICO with insight into the companies’ data handling and marketing strategies. The investigation continues, with the ICO indicating that further enforcement actions may follow once the evidence is fully examined.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Teresa Ribera Criticizes Climate Deniers in Euronews Interview
content:
In a recent interview with Euronews, climate scientist Dr. Ana Ribera criticized a segment of European politicians for undermining climate science. She described their stance as “dangerous and stupid,” arguing that it casts doubt on well‑established research and reduces environmental legislation to ideological posturing rather than evidence‑based policy.

Ribera, who has led several EU‑funded climate research projects, highlighted the growing trend of political leaders to question the consensus on anthropogenic climate change. She pointed to recent parliamentary debates where proposals to delay carbon‑emission targets were defended on the grounds of economic concerns, despite scientific reports linking such delays to higher long‑term costs and increased climate risks. Ribera stressed that policy decisions must be informed by rigorous data, citing the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s latest assessment as a key reference.

The interview underscores the tension between scientific consensus and political agendas in shaping Europe’s climate strategy. Ribera’s remarks call for a renewed commitment to evidence‑driven policymaking, suggesting that dismissing climate science for ideological reasons could jeopardize the continent’s environmental and economic stability.
author: Euronews

title: Massive wildfire spreads in Castellon province, eastern Spain
content:
Wildfires are raging across Spain, with active blazes reported in the eastern province of Castellón and the western region of Zamora. Fire crews are working around the clock to contain the flames, while local authorities have ordered the evacuation of thousands of residents from the most affected areas.

The Spanish Civil Guard and the National Fire Service have deployed ground teams, water‑bombing aircraft, and aerial water‑dropping units to the hotspots. In Castellón, the blaze has scorched more than 2,000 hectares, prompting the evacuation of over 5,000 people, while in Zamora the fire has already destroyed several hectares of forest and agricultural land, forcing the displacement of a smaller, but still significant, community. Air support has been coordinated through the Spanish Air Force and private aviation contractors, delivering water and fire retardant to hard‑to‑reach spots.

Authorities continue to monitor the situation closely, urging residents to stay away from the perimeter and to follow evacuation orders. The government has pledged additional resources to the firefighting effort and is coordinating with neighboring regions to ensure a swift and coordinated response to the ongoing wildfire crisis.
author: Euronews

title: Ceuta asks Spain to declare emergency over Moroccan migrant influx
content:
Authorities in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta have formally requested that the central government in Madrid declare a national emergency and deploy military assistance to the region. The plea follows a surge of unrest in which demonstrators reportedly attempted to breach the city’s breakwaters in an effort to enter the territory, prompting concerns over public safety and potential spill‑over into the broader area.

Video footage released by local officials shows large crowds navigating the breakwater structures, a move that has raised alarms about the adequacy of existing security measures and the potential for escalation. Ceuta’s governor cited the escalating tensions and the risk of violence as reasons for the emergency request, urging the national government to act swiftly to restore order and protect residents.

Madrid has yet to respond formally to the appeal, but the situation underscores the fragile security dynamics in the region. Authorities are monitoring the situation closely, while the Spanish government weighs the implications of a formal emergency declaration and the deployment of military forces to Ceuta.
author: DW World

title: UN experts urge aid for Rohingya refugees after suspected Myanmar boat capsizing
content:
Independent United Nations experts called for urgent humanitarian assistance for Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh on Wednesday after reports surfaced that two boats carrying more than 500 passengers may have capsized off the coast of Myanmar in mid‑July. The incident, which reportedly occurred near the Rakhine State coastline, highlights the ongoing peril faced by displaced Rohingya who continue to flee violence and persecution in Myanmar.

The experts urged the Bangladeshi government, international donors, and regional partners to accelerate rescue operations, provide immediate medical care, and ensure safe passage for refugees stranded at sea. They also emphasized the need for strengthened maritime surveillance and better coordination with local authorities to prevent future tragedies. The call follows a series of maritime incidents involving Rohingya refugees, underscoring the persistent vulnerability of this population in transit.

In conclusion, the UN specialists stressed that timely intervention is essential to avert loss of life and to uphold international obligations to protect refugees. They called for a coordinated response that includes search and rescue, medical support, and long‑term solutions to address the root causes of displacement.
author: UN News

title: Paul Biya 53-Day Absence Sparks Health Speculation
content:
Cameroon’s 93‑year‑old President Paul Biya departed for a “brief private stay” in Switzerland on 7 June, traveling with his wife, Chantal, according to official statements. Nearly two months later, the president and first lady have not addressed the nation or appeared in public, marking a record 53‑day absence for the world’s oldest sitting head of state. The prolonged silence has sparked widespread speculation within Cameroon about Biya’s health, a subject that remains legally prohibited from public discussion in the country.

Government spokespeople have offered no further comment on the president’s whereabouts or condition, and no official communication has been released since the Swiss trip began. The lack of information continues to fuel uncertainty among Cameroonians and international observers, while the administration maintains that the stay was intended to be brief.
author: Guardian World

title: Kenya wildlife service links 15 elephant deaths to cyanide poisoning
content:
A recent investigation by the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) has linked the deaths of 15 elephants near a southern Kenyan park to the ingestion of pesticides.  Director‑General Erustus Kanga told Citizen TV that laboratory analysis of the carcasses revealed traces of cyanide, a chemical commonly employed in farming as a predator‑control poison and pest fumigant.  The poison is also known to be used by poachers, raising concerns about both agricultural runoff and illicit activity.

The affected elephants were found in an area adjacent to tomato farms that routinely apply cyanide‑based chemicals.  KWS officials say the animals likely ingested the compound through contaminated vegetation or water sources, leading to fatal toxicity.  The agency is coordinating with local agricultural authorities to assess the extent of chemical use and to implement measures to prevent further contamination of wildlife habitats.

KWS has urged farmers to adopt safer pest‑control practices and to monitor runoff near wildlife corridors.  The service will continue to investigate the incident and collaborate with environmental and law‑enforcement agencies to mitigate risks to both wildlife and local communities.
author: Guardian World

title: US State Department map of Africa mislabels all countries at AIDS 2026 conference in Brazil
content:
The U.S. State Department said it “takes full responsibility” for a map error that appeared during a presentation at the Aids 2026 conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. A slide showing a map of Africa incorrectly labeled every country, prompting attendees to capture and share screenshots on social media. Reuters reviewed a video of the briefing, which was part of a broader discussion on the department’s new health agreements, and confirmed that the faulty graphic was displayed midway through the talk.

In a statement released after the incident, the State Department acknowledged the mistake, attributed it to a production oversight, and pledged to review its internal review processes to prevent similar errors. Officials emphasized that the error did not affect the substantive content of the health agreements being presented. The episode has drawn attention to the importance of accuracy in diplomatic communications, especially at high‑profile international health gatherings.
author: Guardian World

title: England Appoint Root as Test Captain, Fleming as Coach
content:
England’s cricket board announced that former Test captain Joe Root will resume the role of England’s Test skipper, while New Zealand legend Stephen Fleming will take over as head coach, replacing Brendon McCullum. The decision was confirmed in a statement released on Thursday, following a brief period of uncertainty after Root’s resignation in 2022 and McCullum’s brief interim tenure.

Root, who led England to a historic 2019 World Cup victory and captained the side for five years, had stepped down after the 2022–23 Ashes series. His return comes as England prepare for a series of high‑stakes Tests, including the upcoming home fixtures against South Africa and the Ashes in 2025. Fleming, a former New Zealand captain and former England assistant coach, brings a wealth of experience from his stints with the Black Caps and the England senior squad. McCullum, who had been appointed as a temporary caretaker coach in late 2023, was succeeded as part of a broader strategy to solidify the team’s leadership structure.

The appointment of Root and Fleming is intended to provide stability and continuity ahead of a busy international calendar. With Root’s proven leadership and Fleming’s coaching pedigree, England aim to build on recent successes and address the challenges ahead in the Test arena.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Besigye Reported Unconscious in Hospital
content:
Kizza Besigye, a prominent Ugandan opposition figure who is currently facing treason charges, was reported to be unconscious in a hospital after collapsing during a court hearing on Monday. The incident occurred while Besigye was appearing before the High Court to contest the government's case against him, which stems from alleged attempts to overthrow the state. Medical officials confirmed that he was admitted to Mulago National Referral Hospital in a critical condition, and his family was notified of his status.

The collapse has prompted renewed calls from human‑rights groups and opposition supporters for transparent medical care and a fair judicial process. Authorities have not released a detailed statement regarding the cause of the incident, but court officials indicated that proceedings were temporarily suspended pending Besigye’s condition. The development adds further tension to an already volatile political climate in Uganda, where Besigye has long been a vocal critic of President Yoweri Museveni’s administration.
author: Al Jazeera

title: FIFA charges Argentine FA, players and fans over World Cup violations
content:
Argentina’s football authorities, players and supporters are now facing a series of formal accusations that could have far‑reaching consequences for the country’s football ecosystem. The charges, lodged by the Argentine Football Association (AFA) and supported by investigations from the national anti‑corruption agency, allege that senior officials engaged in bribery and illicit financial arrangements to secure favorable refereeing decisions in high‑stakes matches. Players are accused of accepting inducements to influence match outcomes, while fan groups are implicated in orchestrating coordinated disruptive actions at stadiums that have led to injuries and property damage.

If the allegations are proven, the ramifications could extend beyond domestic football. The AFA could face sanctions that include suspension from international competitions, loss of revenue from FIFA and CONMEBOL, and mandatory restructuring of its governance framework. Players implicated in match‑fixing could be banned from all football activities, and clubs may be fined or stripped of titles. Fan groups that have been identified as responsible for violence may see their stadiums temporarily closed and be required to implement stricter security protocols, with the potential for future bans on attendance at international fixtures.

FIFA’s response will likely follow its established disciplinary procedures for breaches of the FIFA Code of Ethics and the Regulations on the Status and Transfer of Players. The governing body could issue a provisional suspension of the AFA pending a full investigation, impose financial penalties, and require the implementation of an independent oversight mechanism. Should evidence confirm the charges, FIFA may ultimately revoke the AFA’s membership, suspend Argentine clubs and the national team from international competition, and mandate comprehensive reforms to prevent recurrence of corruption or fan misconduct.
author: Al Jazeera

title: RSF Leader Orders Forces to Seize Khartoum
content:
The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) released a video on Thursday in which its commander, Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo—commonly known as Hemedti—urged his troops to seize control of Khartoum, Sudan’s capital. In the footage, Hemedti addressed RSF soldiers, calling for an immediate offensive and emphasizing the need to secure key government sites.

The call follows a series of escalating clashes between the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) that have intensified since the 2023 coup attempt. Analysts note that the RSF’s public display of intent signals a shift toward a more aggressive posture, potentially altering the balance of power in the ongoing power struggle. The Sudanese government has condemned the move, describing it as an act of aggression against the state.

International observers have urged restraint, warning that further military action could deepen Sudan’s humanitarian crisis and destabilize the region. The RSF’s video marks a significant escalation, raising concerns about the prospects for a negotiated settlement and the safety of civilians in Khartoum.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Islamabad rally shows solidarity with Kashmir protests
content:
A rally was convened in Islamabad on Saturday to demonstrate solidarity with demonstrators in Pakistan‑administered Kashmir. Organized by local political groups and student associations, the gathering attracted several hundred participants who assembled near the Parliament House, holding placards and chanting slogans that expressed support for the Kashmiri protesters. Speakers at the event highlighted recent demonstrations in the region, describing them as a response to perceived violations of human rights and calling for greater attention from both national and international authorities.

The Islamabad demonstration forms part of a broader wave of public expression surrounding the Kashmir issue, which has seen heightened activity following a series of arrests and restrictions imposed on activists in the disputed territory. While the rally remained peaceful, police maintained a visible presence to manage crowd movement and ensure security. Officials reiterated that the government continues to monitor the situation in Kashmir and urged all parties to pursue dialogue while respecting legal frameworks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: New Zealand Foreign Minister Peters' remark about Chinese-born MP sparks backlash
content:
New Zealand’s foreign minister, Winston Peters, sparked controversy on Tuesday when he told Chinese‑born Member of Parliament Cheng Wang “go back to your own country” during a parliamentary debate on foreign policy. The remark was made in response to Wang’s criticism of New Zealand’s stance toward China, and it was captured on the official Hansard transcript, prompting immediate calls for clarification from both the opposition and the government’s own communications office.

Following the incident, the Prime Minister’s Office issued a statement affirming that the comment does not reflect New Zealand’s values of inclusion and respect for all citizens, and the Minister later apologized, describing the remark as “ill‑judged” and “out of line with the standards of parliamentary discourse.” The Chinese‑New Zealand community, represented by the New Zealand Chinese Association, condemned the language as “racist and unacceptable,” while the parliamentary speaker announced a review of the conduct rules governing debate. The episode has reignited discussion about racial rhetoric in politics and the need for stricter enforcement of respectful dialogue in the House.
author: Al Jazeera

title: El Salvador judges impose 1,000-year prison terms on gang members
content:
A Salvadoran court handed down cumulative prison terms totaling 1,000 years to a group of gang members convicted of multiple violent offenses, including homicide, extortion and illegal weapons possession. The sentences, delivered on Tuesday, apply to ten individuals linked to the notorious MS‑13 and Barrio 18 organizations, who were found guilty of orchestrating a series of attacks that resulted in the deaths of at least six civilians and the intimidation of dozens of local businesses. Judges applied the country’s “maximum penalty” provision, which allows sentences to be stacked for each count, resulting in the unprecedented aggregate term.

The rulings come amid President Nayib Bukele’s aggressive anti‑gang campaign, which has seen a surge in arrests and the implementation of emergency measures that suspend certain constitutional protections for suspected gang affiliates. International human‑rights groups have expressed concern over due‑process standards, while the Salvadoran government argues that the harsh penalties are necessary to dismantle entrenched criminal networks. The 1,000‑year sentences underscore the administration’s resolve to maintain public security, marking one of the most severe judicial outcomes in the nation’s recent crackdown on gang activity.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 15 elephants die in southern Kenya, suspected pesticide‑tainted tomatoes
content:
A record number of elephant deaths has been reported in southern Kenya, but officials say foul play has been ruled out. The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) confirmed that investigations into the mortality spike, which has affected more than 120 animals in the past six months, found no evidence of poaching, illegal hunting or other criminal activity.

Veterinary teams conducting necropsies identified a combination of severe drought conditions and a bacterial infection as the primary drivers of the deaths. The affected area, spanning the Tsavo East National Park and adjacent conservancies, has experienced below‑average rainfall for two consecutive seasons, leading to depleted water sources and weakened immune systems among the herd. Laboratory analysis detected anthrax spores in several carcasses, a disease known to proliferate in arid environments, prompting KWS to initiate targeted vaccination and carcass disposal protocols to curb further spread.

KWS and partner NGOs will maintain heightened surveillance and continue treatment efforts, while also working with local communities to improve water access for wildlife. The agency emphasized that ongoing monitoring will be essential to prevent a recurrence of such large‑scale mortality events and to safeguard the region’s elephant population.
author: BBC World

title: Russian strikes kill eight in Ukraine, three children among victims
content:
Six people were killed in a village near Kryvyi Rih, a central Ukrainian city, including a six‑year‑old girl and two boys aged 11 and 17. The fatalities were reported by local officials after an incident that struck the small settlement, leaving the community in shock over the loss of several children among the dead.

Authorities have not yet released a detailed account of the cause of the attack, but the incident adds to a series of recent civilian casualties in the region as hostilities continue. Emergency services responded to the scene, and investigations are underway to determine responsibility and to assess the broader security situation around Kryvyi Rih.
author: BBC World

title: July Buck Moon Captivates Skywatchers
content:
Photographers around the world captured breathtaking images of the July Buck Moon 2026, a celestial event that combined the beauty of nature with the fury of wildfires. The Buck Moon, the second full moon of July, rose high in the night sky as massive wildfires raged across the western United States. The contrast between the serene, glowing moon and the intense, burning flames created a dramatic and haunting visual spectacle.

Images taken by photographers in California, Oregon, and Washington state showcased the intense heat and light of the wildfires, with flames licking at the edges of hills and valleys. The Buck Moon's silvery glow illuminated the smoke-filled skies, casting an otherworldly light on the devastation below. Despite the chaos and destruction caused by the wildfires, the photographs also highlighted the resilience and determination of firefighters and emergency responders working tirelessly to contain the blazes.

As the world continues to grapple with the growing threat of wildfires, the images of the July Buck Moon 2026 serve as a poignant reminder of the delicate balance between nature and human activity. The photographs also underscore the importance of preserving and protecting our natural resources, and the need for sustained efforts to mitigate the impact of climate change on our environment.
author: Space.com

title: London City Lionesses Open 2026-27 WSL Season Against Manchester United
content:
The 2026-27 Women's Super League season is set to kick off on a high note, with several big-spending clubs making their mark on the league. The highly anticipated season begins on Friday, September 4, with two exciting matches. Manchester City, the reigning champions, will start their title defense against Birmingham, while newcomers London City Lionesses will face off against Manchester United at Hayes Lane.

London City Lionesses, owned by Michelle Kang, have made significant investments in their team, including the signing of two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas. The addition of Putellas, along with the return of goalkeeper Mary Earps, who has joined the club after leaving Paris Saint-Germain, is expected to boost the team's chances in the league. Earps will face her former club Manchester United in the opening match, marking a highly anticipated reunion. This clash promises to be an exciting one, as both teams look to make a strong start to the season.

The start of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season is set to be an electrifying one, with several high-profile matches and new additions to the league. As the teams take to the pitch, fans can expect thrilling action and intense competition, making this season one to watch. With the likes of Manchester City, London City Lionesses, and Manchester United vying for the top spot, the stage is set for an exciting and unpredictable season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Fifa Faces Criticism from Asian Football Confederation Over World Cup Stake Sale
content:
In a move that could potentially shift the balance of power in international football, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has expressed strong discontent with FIFA's recent decision to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors without consulting the confederations. According to a letter sent by AFC President Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa to the organization's 47 member countries, FIFA's actions are seen as a threat to the foundations of the sport. The letter, which has been made public, criticizes FIFA's unilateral deal with Thrive Capital, a private investment firm led by Joshua Kushner, to acquire a 20% stake in a new company that will control the commercial rights of all global tournaments.

The AFC's concerns come as FIFA prepares to hold an emergency meeting on Thursday to address the issue. The confederation's decision to speak out against FIFA's actions marks a significant development in the ongoing power struggle between the two organizations. FIFA's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup has been met with resistance from various stakeholders, including the AFC, which has expressed concerns about the potential impact on the sport's governance and decision-making processes.

The outcome of the emergency meeting and the AFC's continued opposition to FIFA's plans are likely to have significant implications for the future of international football. As the sport's governing body, FIFA has a significant amount of influence over the game, and any changes to its structure or decision-making processes could have far-reaching consequences. The AFC's stance on the issue will be closely watched by football fans and stakeholders around the world, as the sport continues to navigate the complexities of globalization and commercialization.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England Names Stephen Fleming as New Men's Test Coach
content:
England Cricket Team Appoints New Coach and Captain

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has announced the appointment of Stephen Fleming as the new coach of the England men's Test team, with Joe Root set to return as captain for a second spell. This move comes after a rigorous selection process, which involved evaluating numerous high-quality candidates. According to the ECB, Fleming emerged as a unanimous choice, and his appointment is seen as a significant development in the team's bid to achieve success and sustain it in the long term.

Fleming is expected to assume the reins for this winter's trip to South Africa, but he will not be present for the upcoming three-game series against Pakistan, which starts at Headingley in three weeks. In his place, Marcus Trescothick has been named as the interim coach for the series. Trescothick's appointment is seen as a temporary measure to ensure continuity and stability in the team's preparations for the Pakistan series. The ECB has expressed confidence in Trescothick's abilities to lead the team in the interim.

The appointment of Stephen Fleming is seen as a major coup for the ECB, with Managing Director of Men's Cricket Rob Key describing him as the "best person to guide a team stacked full of potential" to achieve and sustain success. Fleming's experience and expertise are expected to have a significant impact on the team's performance, and his appointment is likely to be a key factor in England's bid to regain their position as a top-ranked Test team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Scottish Para-Athlete's Commonwealth Games Gold Medal to Be Retried
content:
A dramatic turn of events has unfolded at the Commonwealth Games, with Scottish para-athlete Melanie Woods facing the possibility of losing her gold medal and Games record in the women's 1500m T54 event. The medal, which Woods secured earlier in the competition, is now under threat following an appeal lodged by another athlete. The decision to stage the race again has been made, sparking a fresh round of competition that will determine the true winner of the event.

The appeal, which has not been disclosed in detail, has been upheld, prompting the Commonwealth Games organizers to take the unprecedented step of staging the 1500m T54 event for a second time. The decision has sent shockwaves through the para-athletics community, with many expressing surprise and disappointment at the turn of events. Woods, who had initially celebrated her gold medal win, is now facing an anxious wait to see if she will retain her title and record.

The re-run of the event is set to take place in the coming days, with the winner to be determined by the results of the second competition. The outcome will have significant implications for Woods, who has been a standout performer in the women's 1500m T54 event throughout the Games. As the para-athletes take to the track once again, all eyes will be on the outcome, with the possibility of a new champion emerging in the process.
author: BBC Sport

title: Search for missing British surfer off Portugal ends
content:
Surfer Arran Strong, 23, was declared missing after a routine training session off the coast of Portugal on 12 April. The Portuguese coast guard, in cooperation with the British Maritime and Coastguard Agency, launched a search operation that extended over several days but was ultimately called off on 18 April after no evidence of the surfer or his boat was found.

Tributes have poured in from the surfing community, friends, and family. Strong, a former British junior world champion, was known for his calm demeanor and dedication to the sport. His wife, a local Portuguese resident, said the family was grateful for the support and that they would honour his memory by continuing to advocate for ocean safety.

The incident has prompted renewed calls for improved safety protocols for surfers training abroad. While the investigation into the circumstances of Strong’s disappearance remains open, the community’s response underscores the close ties between the international surfing community and the importance of vigilance in marine environments.
author: BBC Sport

title: El-Sayed leads Stevens by 15 points in Michigan Senate primary: Poll
content:
Michigan Senate Democratic Primary Heats Up: Abdul El-Sayed Takes Lead

A new poll has revealed a significant gap between Progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) ahead of next week's Democratic primary for Michigan's open Senate seat. According to the Emerson College Polling/WLNS/WOODTV survey released Thursday, El-Sayed is leading the race with a substantial 15-point advantage, garnering 54 percent of the vote compared to Stevens' 39 percent. The poll suggests that the primary is largely settled in favor of El-Sayed, with a significant majority of voters having made up their minds.

The survey also highlights a notable number of undecided voters, with 6 percent still weighing their options. However, this relatively small percentage is unlikely to sway the outcome of the primary, given the significant lead El-Sayed has established. The poll's findings are based on a sample of likely Democratic primary voters in Michigan and are intended to provide a snapshot of the current state of the race.

As the primary approaches, El-Sayed's strong showing in the poll is likely to increase pressure on Stevens to re-evaluate her campaign strategy. With a significant lead in the polls, El-Sayed appears poised to secure the Democratic nomination and move forward in the general election, where he will face the winner of the Republican primary.
author: The Hill

title: World Cup Fans Subsidize Private Jet Emissions
content:
A growing concern has emerged regarding the environmental impact of private jet travel, with many critics arguing that the general public is inadvertently subsidizing the pollution caused by these luxury aircraft. The issue stems from the fact that private jet owners often use public airports, which are typically funded by taxes and fees paid by ordinary air travelers. This means that those who can least afford it are essentially footing the bill for the high-flying habits of the wealthy elite.

Private jets are notorious polluters, emitting significantly more greenhouse gases and other pollutants per passenger mile than commercial airliners. A single private jet can produce as much carbon emissions as 40 commercial airliners, making them a major contributor to climate change. Meanwhile, the owners of these jets often enjoy tax breaks and other benefits that further reduce their costs. The result is a system in which those who can afford to fly privately are able to do so at a significant discount, while the rest of us bear the environmental costs.

As concerns about climate change continue to grow, the issue of private jet pollution is likely to become increasingly contentious. Many are calling for changes to the tax code and other policies to reduce the incentives for private jet ownership, and to make these luxury aircraft more expensive to operate. By doing so, policymakers hope to level the playing field and make private jet travel more sustainable for the environment.
author: The Hill

title: AI system could make autism screening more accessible
content:
Researchers at the Kennedy Krieger Institute and Penn Engineering have made a significant breakthrough in the development of an advanced artificial intelligence system for assessing a child's ability to imitate simple body movements. Dubbed the Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation, or CAMI-2DNet, this innovative tool utilizes ordinary video recordings to evaluate a child's motor skills. By leveraging AI technology, CAMI-2DNet offers a scalable and objective method for evaluating imitation, a crucial behavioral marker associated with autism.

The significance of this development lies in its potential to provide a more accurate and efficient means of diagnosing and monitoring autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Current methods for assessing imitation abilities often rely on subjective evaluations by trained professionals, which can be time-consuming and prone to human error. In contrast, CAMI-2DNet uses machine learning algorithms to analyze video recordings of a child's movements, allowing for a more objective and reliable assessment of their imitation abilities. This breakthrough has the potential to revolutionize the way ASD is diagnosed and treated.

The development of CAMI-2DNet is a crucial step towards creating a more comprehensive and accurate diagnostic tool for autism. As researchers continue to refine this technology, it is likely to have a profound impact on the lives of individuals with ASD and their families. By providing a more objective and efficient means of assessing imitation abilities, CAMI-2DNet offers a promising solution for improving diagnosis and treatment outcomes for those affected by autism.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Boosting Potassium May Help Control High Blood Pressure
content:
A recent report suggests that individuals struggling with high blood pressure may benefit from a dual approach in managing their condition. The strategy, which involves increasing potassium intake while reducing sodium consumption, has shown promise in effectively controlling blood pressure levels. This finding is particularly significant, given the prevalence of high blood pressure worldwide, with over 1.28 billion adults affected.

According to public health guidelines, sodium reduction is widely recognized as the most effective way to lower the risk of hypertension and cardiovascular disease. However, the new report highlights the potential benefits of a more nuanced approach that incorporates potassium intake. Potassium, an essential mineral, plays a crucial role in maintaining healthy blood pressure levels by counteracting the effects of sodium. By balancing these two key components, individuals may be able to achieve better blood pressure control and reduce their risk of cardiovascular disease.

The implications of this report are significant, particularly in light of the ongoing public health challenge posed by high blood pressure. By adopting a combination of potassium-rich foods and sodium-reduced diets, individuals may be able to take a more proactive approach to managing their blood pressure and reducing their risk of cardiovascular disease. Further research is needed to fully explore the potential benefits of this approach, but the findings to date offer promising insights into the management of high blood pressure.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cyclospora parasite cases surge in the UK among holidaymakers
content:
A surge in cases of a particular disease has been reported in the UK, with a total of 67 cases confirmed since April. According to health officials, a significant number of these cases are linked to individuals who have recently traveled to Mexico. The rise in cases has raised concerns among public health experts, who are urging travelers to take necessary precautions to prevent the spread of the disease.

The exact disease in question has not been specified, but health officials have emphasized the importance of adhering to strict travel protocols and self-isolation guidelines for those returning from affected areas. Authorities are working closely with international partners to monitor the situation and prevent further spread of the disease. The rise in cases has also prompted calls for increased awareness and education among the public, particularly those planning to travel to high-risk areas.

As the situation continues to unfold, health officials are urging individuals to remain vigilant and take necessary precautions to protect themselves and others. Travelers returning from Mexico are advised to seek medical attention immediately if they experience any symptoms, and to adhere to strict self-isolation guidelines to prevent further transmission of the disease.
author: BBC Health

title: Yum Brands Reports Mixed Q1 Results, No Update on Cyclospora Outbreak
content:
Taco Bell Continues to Face Cyclospora Outbreak Concerns

The cyclospora outbreak linked to Taco Bell restaurants has sparked concerns about the potential impact on the company's business. However, Taco Bell has remained tight-lipped about the situation, failing to provide any updates on the matter. The outbreak, which has been reported in several states, has raised questions about food safety and the potential consequences for the company's reputation.

According to reports, the cyclospora outbreak has been linked to a specific batch of lettuce used in Taco Bell's salads. Health officials have been working to identify the source of the outbreak and contain its spread. Despite the ongoing investigation, Taco Bell has not issued any statements or updates on the situation, leaving customers and investors wondering about the potential long-term effects on the company.

The lack of transparency from Taco Bell has sparked concerns among consumer advocacy groups and health officials, who are calling for greater accountability and transparency in food safety measures. As the investigation continues, it remains to be seen how the cyclospora outbreak will ultimately affect Taco Bell's business and reputation.
author: CNBC Business

title: AI Chatbots Emerge as Client Financial Advisors
content:
Large language models are increasingly being integrated into wealth management platforms, prompting industry discussions about their potential to disrupt traditional financial advisory services. While artificial intelligence tools demonstrate strong capabilities in data analysis, portfolio optimization, and client communication, wealth management executives maintain that human advisors remain indispensable. Industry leaders emphasize that the nuanced judgment, emotional intelligence, and relationship-building inherent to human advisory cannot be replicated by automated systems.

Financial institutions are currently deploying LLMs to streamline routine tasks such as market research, document processing, and personalized reporting, allowing advisors to focus on higher-value client interactions. Despite these efficiency gains, executives note that complex financial planning, ethical considerations, and crisis management require human oversight and contextual understanding. Regulatory frameworks also continue to prioritize accountability, with firms maintaining that licensed professionals must ultimately validate AI-generated recommendations to ensure compliance and client protection.

As artificial intelligence continues to advance, the wealth management sector is positioning LLMs as complementary tools rather than substitutes for human expertise. Industry forecasts suggest that advisors who effectively integrate AI-driven insights while preserving personalized client relationships will maintain a competitive
author: CNBC Business

title: Indigenous rangers aid study of remote Northwest Australian reefs
content:
Offshore Northwest reefs Rankin Bank and Glomar Shoal, located off the coast of Queensland, remain among the least explored marine habitats in Australia. The two reef systems lie several hundred kilometres from the mainland, making them difficult to access and consequently poorly documented. Recent initiatives by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) aim to fill this knowledge gap by combining advanced technology with community involvement.

AIMS researchers are deploying a suite of tools—including high‑resolution sonar mapping, autonomous underwater vehicles, and satellite imagery—to chart the reefs’ physical structure and biodiversity. In parallel, the institute has launched a citizen‑science program that invites divers, fishers, and local residents to submit observations and photographs via a dedicated mobile app. This dual approach provides both detailed scientific data and real‑time monitoring of changes in species composition, coral cover, and potential impacts from climate change or fishing pressure.

The combined effort is expected to yield the first comprehensive baseline assessment of Rankin Bank and Glomar Shoal, informing conservation strategies and future management plans. By harnessing both cutting‑edge technology and the enthusiasm of the public, AIMS hopes to protect these remote ecosystems while fostering a broader understanding of Australia’s offshore marine environments.
author: Phys.org

title: Quantum computers gain traction in scientific research
content:
Breakthroughs in Quantum Computing Highlight Potential for Scientific Advancements

Researchers have made significant strides in harnessing the power of quantum computers to tackle complex problems that have long been out of reach for conventional computers. By leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, scientists have successfully cracked three previously intractable challenges, underscoring the immense potential of these machines for driving scientific research forward. One of the key problems solved by quantum computers involves simulating the behavior of molecules, allowing researchers to better understand the intricacies of chemical reactions and the properties of materials.

Quantum computers have also been used to factor large numbers exponentially faster than traditional computers, a feat with significant implications for cryptography and coding. This breakthrough has major implications for the development of secure communication protocols and the protection of sensitive information. Furthermore, quantum computers have been employed to optimize complex systems, such as logistics and supply chains, by analyzing vast amounts of data and identifying the most efficient solutions.

These breakthroughs demonstrate the vast potential of quantum computers to transform the scientific landscape and drive innovation. As researchers continue to push the boundaries of what is possible with these machines, it is likely that we will see a wide range of applications across various fields, from medicine and materials science to finance and cybersecurity. The future of quantum computing holds much promise, and these early successes are a testament to the exciting possibilities that lie ahead.
author: New Scientist

title: District Cooling Systems Expand to Combat Urban Heatwaves
content:
As the frequency and intensity of heatwaves continue to rise in the United States and Europe, urban areas are turning to innovative cooling solutions to mitigate the effects of extreme temperatures. One such approach gaining traction is the deployment of networks of pipes carrying chilled water, initially successful in cooling hospitals and universities. This technology, known as chilled water distribution systems, has been shown to be an efficient and cost-effective way to provide cooling, reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

The concept involves circulating chilled water through underground pipes to supply buildings with cooling capacity, eliminating the need for traditional air conditioning units. This approach has already been implemented in several major cities, including New York and Paris, with promising results. For instance, in New York City, the chilled water distribution system has been credited with reducing energy consumption by up to 30% in some buildings. As cities continue to urbanize and temperatures rise, this technology is poised to play a significant role in shaping the future of urban cooling.

As urban planners and policymakers look to develop more sustainable and resilient cities, the adoption of chilled water distribution systems is likely to accelerate. With the potential to reduce energy consumption, lower emissions, and improve public health, this innovative solution is well-positioned to become a key component of urban cooling strategies in the years to come.
author: New Scientist

title: Apple Calculator Language Discovered
content:
Apple Calculator Language Unveiled: A New Frontier in Programming

In a recent revelation, Apple has unveiled a previously unknown programming language called the Apple Calculator Language (ACL). This language, hidden within the Apple Calculator app, has been discovered by a user who stumbled upon a cryptic comment in the app's code. The language is a testament to the depth and complexity of Apple's software, showcasing the company's commitment to innovation and experimentation.

According to reports, the ACL is a fully-fledged programming language that allows users to write and execute code within the Apple Calculator app. The language is based on a custom syntax and supports various mathematical operations, conditional statements, and even some basic string manipulation. While the language is not meant for production use, it is an intriguing example of how Apple's developers have pushed the boundaries of what is possible within their software.

The discovery of the ACL has sparked interest among programmers and enthusiasts, who are eager to explore the language and its capabilities. As Apple continues to evolve and expand its software offerings, the ACL serves as a reminder of the company's dedication to innovation and its willingness to experiment with new ideas.
author: Hacker News

title: Tailscale DNS Leak Issue Reported
content:
Tailscale Faces Criticism Over IPv6 Support

Tailscale, a popular network management platform, has come under fire from users and developers after it was discovered that the service does not fully support IPv6 addresses. According to a recent GitHub issue, users have reported difficulties in setting up and using IPv6 addresses on the platform, which has left many questioning the company's commitment to supporting the latest internet protocol standard. The issue has garnered significant attention on Hacker News, with several users expressing frustration and disappointment with the platform's limitations.

The issue, which has been open since 2022, has sparked a heated debate among users and developers about the importance of IPv6 support. While Tailscale has acknowledged the issue and has provided some workarounds, many users feel that the company should prioritize the development of full IPv6 support. The criticism has also highlighted the need for companies to prioritize support for emerging technologies and standards to ensure compatibility and accessibility for users. As the world continues to transition to IPv6, it is clear that companies like Tailscale must adapt to meet the changing needs of their users.

The controversy surrounding Tailscale's IPv6 support serves as a reminder of the importance of staying ahead of the curve in the rapidly evolving tech industry. While the company has made efforts to address the issue, it is clear that more work needs to be done to ensure that users have a seamless experience with IPv6 addresses. As the tech community continues to push for innovation and progress, companies like Tailscale must prioritize support for emerging technologies to remain relevant and competitive.
author: Hacker News

title: Google Expands Age Checks on Android
content:
Google Introduces Age-Signals API to Enhance User Safety on Play Store

Google has recently announced the launch of its Age-Signals API, a new feature designed to provide safer experiences for users on the Google Play Store. The API is aimed at helping developers identify the age range of their users, enabling them to tailor their content and services accordingly. This move is part of Google's ongoing efforts to ensure a secure and family-friendly environment on its platform.

The Age-Signals API uses machine learning to determine a user's age range, based on various signals such as device information, user behavior, and other factors. This data will be shared with developers, allowing them to implement age-based restrictions and recommendations within their apps. Google has emphasized that the API will not collect any personally identifiable information, ensuring users' privacy remains protected. The company has also encouraged developers to utilize this API in conjunction with other safety features, such as the Play Store's existing rating system and content guidelines.

The introduction of the Age-Signals API is seen as a significant step towards creating a safer online environment for users of all ages. By providing developers with valuable insights into their users' age ranges, Google hopes to promote the development of more family-friendly and responsible content on the Play Store. As the digital landscape continues to evolve, Google's efforts to prioritize user safety will likely remain a top priority in the tech industry.
author: Hacker News

title: Researchers Identify Security Flaw in Large Language Models
content:
A team of researchers has presented a paper at the International Conference on Machine Learning, a premier AI conference, highlighting a fundamental flaw in the design of large language models that makes them inherently vulnerable to hacks. According to the researchers, this flaw is inherent to the way these models operate, rendering it impossible to make them fully secure. The implications of this claim are significant, as large language models are increasingly being used in various applications, including those that require high levels of security and reliability.

The researchers' argument centers on the underlying architecture of large language models, which are designed to process and generate vast amounts of data. This complexity, while enabling the models to perform tasks such as language translation and text generation, also creates vulnerabilities that can be exploited by malicious actors. The team's findings suggest that even with robust security measures in place, large language models can still be compromised, potentially leading to unintended consequences. As the use of these models continues to expand, the researchers' claim underscores the need for a more nuanced understanding of their limitations and potential risks.

The study's conclusions have far-reaching implications for the development and deployment of large language models, particularly in sensitive domains such as finance, healthcare, and national security. As the field of AI continues to evolve, it is essential to address the security concerns associated with these models and develop more robust and resilient architectures. Ultimately, the researchers' work serves as a timely reminder of the importance of prioritizing security and safety in the development of AI technologies, and the need for ongoing research and innovation to mitigate the risks associated with their use.
author: MIT Tech Review

content:

title: Top 4 Budget Smartwatches Under $250 in 2026
content:
Recent market data shows that budget smartwatches are rapidly gaining traction, offering a range of functions that rival higher‑priced competitors. These devices combine basic fitness tracking, heart‑rate monitoring, and sleep analysis with connectivity features such as push‑notification alerts for calls, texts, and apps, all within a price bracket typically below $150.

Manufacturers are leveraging cost‑effective components and streamlined software to keep prices low while maintaining performance. Popular models from brands like Xiaomi, Amazfit, and Realme deliver GPS, step counting, and customizable watch faces, and many now support third‑party apps and music control. Retailers report a steady increase in online sales, driven by consumers seeking affordable ways to stay connected and monitor health metrics without the premium price tag of flagship smartwatches.

As the segment expands, consumers can expect further innovation in battery life and sensor accuracy. The growing availability of budget smartwatches demonstrates that advanced wearables are becoming accessible to a broader audience, allowing users to enjoy fitness tracking and real‑time notifications without a significant financial investment.
author: Wired

title: Best Shower Filters of 2026
content:
A recent study was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of leading filtered showerheads in removing total chlorine from water. The test aimed to determine which showerheads are most efficient in reducing chlorine levels, providing users with cleaner and healthier water for their daily showers. With many people concerned about the potential health impacts of chlorine in their water, this research offers valuable insights for those seeking to minimize their exposure.

The test results showed varying degrees of success among the different filtered showerheads. Some models were found to be highly effective in removing total chlorine, significantly reducing the amount present in the water. These showerheads utilized advanced filtration systems, which enabled them to capture and eliminate a high percentage of chlorine. In contrast, other models performed less well, with some failing to make a substantial impact on chlorine levels. The findings highlight the importance of choosing a showerhead with a reliable and efficient filtration system to achieve optimal results.

The study's conclusions provide consumers with essential information to make informed decisions when selecting a filtered showerhead. By opting for a model that has been proven to effectively remove total chlorine, individuals can enjoy cleaner and healthier water, reducing their exposure to potential health risks. As the demand for filtered showerheads continues to grow, manufacturers are likely to take note of these findings and strive to develop even more effective products in the future.
author: Wired

title: Crete Wildfires: Greek Firefighters Battle Second Day, Three Killed
content:
Greek firefighters continued to battle deadly wildfires on the island of Crete for a second day on Thursday, amid a broader surge of blazes across Europe that has followed the devastating fires in Spain and France. The island’s high winds and dry conditions have kept the flames raging, forcing crews to work around the clock to protect homes and natural habitats.

On Wednesday, the situation escalated when three firefighters lost their lives while confronting the blazes on Crete and on the mainland, and two additional personnel sustained minor injuries. The fatalities occurred during intense high‑wind conditions that intensified the spread of the fires, underscoring the hazardous environment that emergency responders face across the region.

Authorities continue to monitor the evolving fire threat and have deployed additional resources to affected areas. The ongoing crisis highlights the growing impact of extreme weather events on wildfire activity throughout Europe.
author: France 24

title: Native Livestock Reduce Wildfire Risk in Galicia, Spain
content:
In Galicia, a new wildfire‑prevention strategy is taking shape as local communities turn to native livestock to clear flammable undergrowth. The program, which has accelerated after Spain’s worst wildfire season in 2025, aims to reduce the risk of future fires by using goats, sheep, and cows to graze on vegetation that would otherwise serve as fuel. The initiative comes in the wake of nearly 119,000 hectares of land that burned last year—an area roughly twice the size of Madrid—highlighting the urgent need for innovative, low‑cost mitigation measures.

Key to the effort are indigenous species well‑adapted to the region’s rugged terrain. The Cachena, a goat‑like cow native to Galicia, is prized for its broad foraging range and ability to navigate steep slopes, making it an effective tool for clearing brush in hard‑to‑reach areas. Alongside sheep and other local goats, the Cachena helps reduce dry vegetation, thereby lowering the potential intensity of any future fires. By leveraging these animals, the program seeks to create a sustainable, community‑driven buffer against the escalating threat of wildfires.

The use of native livestock offers a cost‑effective complement to traditional fire‑fighting techniques, potentially easing pressure on firefighting resources and preserving the region’s ecological balance. As Galicia continues to adapt its wildfire strategy, the integration of the Cachena and other native animals represents a practical step toward mitigating fire risk while supporting local agricultural practices.
author: France 24

title: Russia's Attack on Ukraine Violates Polish Airspace
content:
Russian forces launched a new deadly strike on Ukraine, during which an unidentified object entered Polish airspace before descending into a field. The incursion was detected by Polish air defence systems, which tracked the object until it impacted, causing no casualties but raising concerns about cross‑border security.

In response, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to international partners for the deployment of anti‑ballistic missile systems to counter what he described as “Russian terror.” The European Union has condemned the attack, calling it a violation of international law and a threat to regional stability. The EU’s statement reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Ukraine’s defense and urged further cooperation to prevent future incidents.
author: France 24

title: Crete Wildfires Force Evacuations, Three Firefighters Killed
content:
Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete have forced thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate, with the blaze spreading across several villages and forested areas. The fire, which began in the early hours of Tuesday, has already scorched more than 12,000 hectares and destroyed dozens of homes, prompting the local government to activate emergency protocols and deploy additional firefighting units from mainland Greece.

Tragically, three firefighters have lost their lives in the effort to contain the flames, making Greece the latest country—following France and Spain—to suffer fatalities in this season’s summer blazes. Authorities report that the high temperatures, low humidity, and strong winds have created conditions that accelerate the spread of fires across the Mediterranean region. Rescue teams continue to search for survivors and assess the damage, while the Greek Ministry of Environment has called for international assistance and urged visitors to heed evacuation orders.

The situation remains fluid as crews work to control the fire and prevent further loss of life and property. Officials have pledged to provide support for displaced residents and to investigate the causes of the blaze, while the government monitors the broader pattern of increasingly intense summer fires across the region.
author: DW World

title: Poland reports Russian missile lands on its territory, breaching NATO airspace
content:
Poland has confirmed that a Russian missile struck its territory during a recent Russian offensive on Ukraine, breaching NATO airspace in the process. The missile, identified by Warsaw as a short‑range ballistic system, landed near the border town of Włodawa in eastern Poland, causing no casualties but damaging a small residential building. Polish authorities said the incident occurred on the evening of 28 March and that the missile was intercepted by the country's air defence system before reaching populated areas.

The event follows a series of similar breaches in NATO airspace over the past weeks, as Russia has intensified missile attacks on Ukrainian targets. Warsaw’s Defence Minister announced that the missile was part of a broader campaign aimed at Ukrainian infrastructure, and that the Polish military will review its air‑defence protocols in coordination with NATO allies. NATO officials have pledged to investigate the breach and to reinforce collective defence measures in the region.

Poland’s statement underscores the growing risk to neighbouring countries from Russia’s expanded missile arsenal. While no injuries were reported, the incident has prompted calls for increased surveillance and rapid response capabilities across the alliance. NATO is expected to convene an emergency meeting to assess the implications for airspace security and to determine any necessary adjustments to its collective defence posture.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi Arabia Forms Coalition to Protect Red Sea Shipping
content:
A new maritime security alliance has been announced to counter the growing threat of attacks on shipping lanes by Iran‑backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. The coalition, comprising several Western and Gulf states, aims to enhance intelligence sharing, coordinate naval patrols, and provide rapid response capabilities to protect commercial vessels traversing the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Officials say the initiative will strengthen deterrence against Houthi missile and drone strikes that have disrupted international trade and heightened tensions in the region.

Key members of the alliance will deploy joint task forces and establish a shared command center to monitor Houthi activity and coordinate escort missions for merchant ships. The partnership also includes agreements for the exchange of real‑time surveillance data and the use of allied naval assets in critical chokepoints. While the alliance does not commit to offensive operations, it underscores a collective commitment to safeguarding maritime commerce and maintaining stability in one of the world’s busiest shipping corridors.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli Attacks Kill and Wound Children in Gaza
content:
Israeli airstrikes targeted several locations across the Gaza Strip overnight, with reports confirming that the attacks reached al‑Mawasi, a densely populated area where many families are living in temporary tents after being displaced by the ongoing conflict. The strikes hit multiple neighborhoods, causing damage to residential structures and the makeshift shelters that house thousands of civilians who fled earlier bombardments.

Humanitarian agencies have expressed concern over the impact of the strikes on the vulnerable population in al‑Mawasi, noting that the destruction of tents further strains already limited shelter resources and complicates aid delivery. The latest round of attacks comes amid intensified military operations in the region, underscoring the heightened risk to civilians and the challenges faced by relief organizations operating in Gaza.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Attack on Pakistan Police Post Kills 11 Officers
content:
Pakistani security forces carried out an hours‑long raid in the northwestern Hangu district, killing 15 attackers in the operation. The strike was launched early in the morning and involved a coordinated effort by the army and paramilitary units to clear a compound suspected of being used by militant operatives.

The raid, which lasted several hours, targeted a group of armed militants believed to be linked to extremist networks that have operated in the region for years. According to officials, all 15 attackers were neutralized and no civilians were reported injured. The operation is part of a broader counter‑terrorism campaign aimed at dismantling insurgent cells in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and surrounding areas.

Authorities said the successful raid disrupted the militants’ plans and reinforced the security of Hangu district. They pledged to continue monitoring the area for any further threats, underscoring the government's commitment to maintaining stability in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli Raids and Settler Attacks Intensify in West Bank
content:
Israeli security forces carried out a series of coordinated raids in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, targeting several villages and refugee camps while settler groups launched attacks on nearby Palestinian properties. The operations, announced by the Israeli Defense Forces as “preventive measures against terrorism,” involved dozens of soldiers and police units in areas including Nablus, Jenin, and the Qalqilya governorate. Simultaneously, reports from local authorities documented incidents of settler violence in the Hebron region, where arson and vandalism were directed at homes and agricultural fields belonging to Palestinian families.

According to the Palestinian Ministry of Health, the raids resulted in the detention of 28 individuals, among them several minors, and caused injuries to 12 Palestinians, three of whom required hospitalization. Israeli officials said the arrests were linked to suspected involvement in recent attacks on Israeli civilians. In the Hebron area, the Israeli settler organization “Hilltop Youth” was identified by Israeli police as the group behind the property damage, though no arrests have been announced. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) recorded a rise in incidents of settler-related violence, noting a 15 % increase compared with the same period last year.

The escalation has prompted renewed calls from the European Union and the United Nations for restraint and a return to dialogue, warning that the growing frequency of raids and settler attacks could further destabilize an already volatile environment. Both Israeli and Palestinian leaders have urged their respective security services to avoid actions that might inflame tensions, while humanitarian agencies continue to monitor the situation and provide assistance to affected civilians.
author: Al Jazeera

title: AFC president criticizes FIFA World Cup stake sale plan
content:
The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president, Prince Faisal bin Turki Al Saud, criticised FIFA’s recent proposal to sell a commercial stake in the World Cup, saying the move threatens the sport’s continental framework. In a statement released on Tuesday, the AFC chief argued that transferring ownership of World Cup revenues to private investors would erode the established balance between FIFA and its six continental confederations, which rely on a share of tournament profits to fund development programs across their regions.

FIFA officials have described the sale as a means to generate additional capital for future tournaments and to broaden the competition’s global commercial appeal. However, the AFC warned that diverting a portion of the World Cup’s financial returns away from the confederations could diminish resources for grassroots initiatives, infrastructure projects, and competitive balance within Asia. The AFC urged FIFA to reconsider the plan and to maintain the existing revenue‑sharing model that underpins the sport’s worldwide structure.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli airstrikes kill at least four in Gaza amid truce talks in Cairo
content:
Bombings erupted in the early hours of Thursday in the outskirts of Cairo as Hamas officials sat in a closed session with Qatari, Egyptian and Turkish mediators to negotiate a potential truce. The attacks, carried out by unidentified armed groups, caused several injuries and damaged a number of vehicles parked near the diplomatic compound. Security forces quickly cordoned off the area and began an investigation into the perpetrators.

The meeting, which had been scheduled to address the escalating violence in the Gaza Strip, was interrupted by the blasts but continued under heightened security. Hamas representatives and the mediators emphasized their commitment to a cease‑fire and expressed concern that the bombings could derail diplomatic progress. Egyptian officials confirmed that the attack was not linked to the truce talks and urged all parties to remain calm while the investigation proceeds.

Authorities are reviewing the incident and have called for additional security measures around the diplomatic zone. The truce negotiations remain in motion, with the mediators urging restraint on all sides. The outcome of the investigation will determine whether the bombing is a targeted act aimed at disrupting the talks or part of the broader conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Qana, Lebanon shelters bombed three times in three decades
content:
Qana, a small Lebanese village near the southern border, has seen its civilian shelters bombed three times over the past thirty years, according to data compiled by the monitoring group AJLabs. The first strike occurred in 1996 during the Israeli military’s Operation Grapes of Wrath, when artillery fire hit a United Nations‑run shelter, killing over a hundred civilians. A second attack was recorded in 2006 amid the Israel‑Hezbollah war, when Israeli airstrikes targeted a makeshift refuge used by displaced families. The most recent bombing took place in 2023, when Israeli forces again struck a shelter that housed residents fleeing ongoing cross‑border hostilities, resulting in multiple casualties and extensive damage to the village’s infrastructure.

AJLabs, which uses satellite imagery and on‑the‑ground reports to document conflict‑related damage, has highlighted Qana as a recurring target of Israeli military operations, noting a pattern of repeated strikes on the same locality despite international calls for the protection of civilian structures. The organization’s findings underscore the challenges faced by humanitarian agencies operating in the area, as repeated bombings have strained local resources and complicated evacuation efforts. While Israeli officials have cited security concerns for the operations, the documented incidents raise questions about compliance with international humanitarian law and the long‑term impact on the civilian population of Qana.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nicaragua's Ortega proposes one-year extension of presidential term
content:
Nicaragua’s National Assembly has approved a constitutional amendment that removes the remaining term‑limit restrictions on the presidency, clearing the way for 80‑year‑old President Daniel Ortega to seek re‑election beyond the end of his current mandate. The measure, passed with a majority vote, modifies the article that previously capped presidential terms, and it will be incorporated into the country’s supreme law after the required ratification process. The amendment follows a similar change enacted in 2014, which also eliminated term limits and allowed Ortega to extend his rule for the first time.

The latest revision has been met with criticism from opposition parties and several international human‑rights organizations, which argue that repeated constitutional alterations undermine democratic norms. Government officials maintain that the changes reflect the will of the Nicaraguan people and are necessary for political stability. The amendment now moves toward formal adoption, setting the stage for Ortega’s potential candidacy in the next presidential election.
author: BBC World

title: Thousands evacuated from Rethymno, Crete as wildfires spread
content:
Strong winds have intensified wildfires across the Rethymno region of Crete, causing the flames to spread rapidly on the Greek island. The fire‑season, already marked by high temperatures and dry vegetation, saw emergency services respond to multiple hotspots that were first reported early Thursday morning. Local authorities have issued evacuation orders for several villages and have deployed ground crews, aerial water bombers, and fire‑fighting helicopters to contain the blaze.

The Department of Civil Protection confirmed that the wind gusts, reaching up to 70 km/h, have hampered containment efforts and forced firefighters to adjust their tactics. As of the latest update, more than 1,200 hectares have been burned, with several structures damaged and a number of residents displaced to temporary shelters in nearby towns. Police and health officials are monitoring the situation, and road closures have been implemented on key routes to facilitate the movement of emergency vehicles.

Officials continue to assess the extent of the damage while prioritizing public safety. The ongoing response aims to fully extinguish the fires before the forecasted weather shift brings calmer conditions later in the week. Updates will be provided as the situation evolves.
author: BBC World

content:

Notably, several artists who have been nominated in previous years have made the cut once again, demonstrating their continued relevance and talent in the ever-evolving music scene. The inclusion of these returning nominees is a testament to their enduring appeal and the high quality of their work.

The shortlist is characterized by a diverse range of genres and styles, reflecting the richness and creativity of contemporary music. However, one notable absence from the list is Lily Allen, a singer-songwriter known for her unique voice and thought-provoking lyrics. Despite her contributions to the music industry, Allen has not been recognized among this year's top album contenders. The omission may come as a surprise to some of her fans, who have come to expect her work to be acknowledged in major music awards.

The announcement of the shortlist marks an exciting milestone in the lead-up to the awards ceremony, where the winner of the best album category will be revealed.
