As music enthusiasts eagerly await the outcome, the shortlisted artists are likely to experience a surge in interest and attention, with their work being scrutinized and celebrated by fans and critics alike. The winner will be chosen based on the quality and impact of their album, and the competition is expected to be fierce, given the exceptional talent represented on the shortlist.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Littler and Pogacar Dominate Their Respective Sports
content:
The world of professional darts was abuzz on Sunday night as the World Matchplay final took center stage on Sky Sports. Renowned commentator Wayne Mardle provided insightful analysis, highlighting the key characteristics that set champion darts players apart from their competitors. According to Mardle, the greatest champions possess a unique blend of skill, strategy, and mental toughness, which enables them to capitalize on their opponents' weaknesses and seize victory.

Mardle's commentary shed light on the psychological aspect of the game, where top players must be able to sense their opponents' doubts and vulnerabilities, and then exploit them to gain a competitive edge. This ability to recognize and pounce on weakness is a hallmark of champion darts players, who must balance their own strengths with a deep understanding of their opponents' mental and emotional states. The commentator cited the example of a player achieving a remarkable 167 checkout, despite their opponent being poised to take the lead, as a testament to the mental fortitude and cunning required to succeed at the highest level.

The World Matchplay final served as a showcase for the exceptional skills and competitive drive of the world's top darts players, with Mardle's commentary offering a nuanced perspective on the mental and emotional dynamics at play. As the tournament came to a close, it was clear that the champions who emerged victorious were not only highly skilled technicians, but also masters of the psychological game, able to navigate the complexities of their opponents' minds and emerge triumphant.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Eddie Howe Departs Newcastle United
content:
Eddie Howe has parted ways with Newcastle after a five-year tenure as the club's manager, marking a significant change in the team's leadership. The decision comes as a surprise, given the timing, but it is understood that Howe's position had been under intense scrutiny from the club's Saudi Arabian owners for some time. Despite his efforts to steer the team forward, the owners' expectations and demands ultimately led to his departure from St James' Park.

Matthias Jaissle, the current coach of Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli, is reportedly in line to take over as Newcastle's new manager. A German national, Jaissle has been making a name for himself in the coaching world, and his experience in the Saudi Arabian league could prove valuable in navigating the complexities of managing a high-profile club like Newcastle. As the club embarks on a new chapter, the appointment of Jaissle is expected to bring a fresh perspective and approach to the team's strategy and performance.

The sudden change in management raises questions about the club's future direction and prospects. However, with Jaissle poised to take the reins, Newcastle's owners are likely seeking to inject new energy and momentum into the team. As the football community waits to see how this development unfolds, one thing is certain – the departure of Eddie Howe and the potential arrival of Matthias Jaissle mark a significant turning point in Newcastle's history, and all eyes will be on the club to see how they navigate this transition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: De Zerbi to Talk to Spence About Future
content:
Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto de Zerbi has expressed his desire to persuade England defender Djed Spence to remain at the club. This comes as Spence has been subject to speculation regarding his future, with various reports suggesting he may be considering a move away from Tottenham. De Zerbi's statement indicates that the club values Spence's contributions and is keen to retain his services.

De Zerbi's intention to convince Spence to stay is likely driven by the defender's potential and the important role he could play in the team's future. Spence has shown promise in his appearances for Tottenham, and his ability to represent England at the international level is a testament to his talent. By retaining Spence, Tottenham would be able to maintain continuity and depth in their defense, which could be crucial in their pursuit of success in upcoming seasons. The club's efforts to persuade Spence to stay will likely involve discussions about his role in the team and the opportunities available to him at Tottenham.

In conclusion, Roberto de Zerbi's comments highlight Tottenham's desire to keep Djed Spence at the club, and the manager's efforts to convince the defender to stay will be closely watched in the coming weeks. The outcome of these discussions will have implications for Tottenham's squad and their preparations for the upcoming season, and fans will be eager to learn about Spence's decision regarding his future at the club.
author: BBC Sport

title: Eddie Howe to Leave Newcastle
content:
Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is reportedly set to depart the club with immediate effect, according to sources close to the matter. This development comes as a surprise, given Howe's significant efforts to transform the team since his appointment. The news has sent shockwaves throughout the football community, with fans and pundits alike eager to learn more about the circumstances surrounding his sudden exit.

Details regarding the reasons behind Howe's departure are still scarce, but it is understood that the decision has been made and will be formalized shortly. During his tenure, Howe worked tirelessly to improve the team's performance, implementing a distinct playing style and overseeing notable transfers. His dedication and expertise have been widely acknowledged, making his abrupt departure all the more unexpected. As the club prepares to move forward, attention will turn to the process of identifying and appointing a suitable successor to take the reins.

The search for a new manager is likely to commence immediately, with the club seeking a candidate who can build upon the foundations laid by Howe and drive the team towards future success. As the situation continues to unfold, Newcastle supporters will be watching with great interest, hoping for a seamless transition and a positive outcome for the club. With the football season in full swing, the club's hierarchy will be keen to resolve the managerial situation swiftly, ensuring that the team can maintain focus and momentum on the pitch.
author: BBC Sport

title: Fauci Faces Senate Hearing
content:
In a recent hearing, lawmakers engaged in contentious questioning of Dr. Anthony Fauci, the former top US Health official. The exchange, which took place on Wednesday, has drawn significant attention and sparked discussions about the role of health officials in shaping the country's response to public health crises. Dr. Céline Gounder, a prominent expert in the field, shared her insights on the matter with NPR's Michel Martin, providing context and analysis of the tense exchange.

Dr. Gounder's conversation with Michel Martin shed light on the complexities and challenges faced by health officials like Dr. Fauci, who have been at the forefront of the country's response to major health crises. The questioning of Dr. Fauci by lawmakers reflects the intense scrutiny and politicization of public health issues, highlighting the difficulties that health officials face in communicating scientific information and guiding policy decisions. Dr. Gounder's expertise and perspective helped to illuminate the nuances of the situation, providing a deeper understanding of the issues at play and the implications for the country's public health landscape.

The discussion between Dr. Gounder and Michel Martin serves as a reminder of the importance of informed and respectful dialogue in addressing complex public health issues. As the country continues to navigate the challenges of emerging health crises, the need for clear communication, scientific expertise, and collaborative decision-making has never been more pressing. The exchange between lawmakers and Dr. Fauci, and the subsequent analysis by Dr. Gounder, underscores the critical role that health officials and experts play in shaping the national conversation around public health, and the need for ongoing efforts to promote understanding, cooperation, and effective policy responses.
author: NPR Politics

title: Lanthanide carriers improve biomedical imaging and theranostics
content:
Lanthanide‑based carriers are emerging as a promising tool for the next generation of biomedical imaging, offering a pathway to accelerate the development of theranostics—a field that combines diagnostic imaging with targeted treatment. By harnessing the unique optical, magnetic, and luminescent properties of lanthanide elements, researchers can create contrast agents that provide clearer, more specific imaging signals while simultaneously delivering therapeutic agents to diseased tissues.

These carriers can be engineered to bind selectively to biomarkers on cancer cells, inflammatory sites, or other pathological tissues, enabling high‑resolution imaging through techniques such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), fluorescence imaging, or computed tomography. In addition, the same platform can be loaded with drugs, radioisotopes, or gene‑editing tools, allowing clinicians to monitor drug distribution and efficacy in real time. Early preclinical studies have demonstrated that lanthanide carriers reduce off‑target toxicity and improve the signal‑to‑noise ratio compared with conventional agents, thereby enhancing both diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic precision.

The integration of lanthanide carriers into theranostic workflows could shorten the time from diagnosis to treatment, streamline clinical decision‑making, and ultimately improve patient outcomes. As regulatory pathways and manufacturing processes mature, these advanced carriers may soon transition from laboratory prototypes to routine clinical tools, redefining how imaging and therapy are coordinated in modern medicine.
author: Medical Xpress

title: France and Spain Forest Fires Subside
content:
A massive forest fire in France, which had been raging out of control, appears to be coming under control, with firefighters expressing optimism that the blaze is no longer spreading. This development comes as a welcome relief, as the fire had been causing significant concern and damage to the surrounding area. The efforts of the firefighters, who have been working tirelessly to contain the fire, seem to be paying off, and the situation is being closely monitored to ensure that the fire does not flare up again.

In a similar situation, Spain has reported that a forest fire near Madrid, which had been burning intensely, has almost been completely extinguished. According to Spanish authorities, there are now "almost no flames" left, indicating that the fire is all but under control. This is a significant development, as the fire had been causing widespread damage and disruption to the area. The progress made in containing the fires in both France and Spain is a testament to the hard work and dedication of the firefighters and emergency services, who have been working to bring the situation under control.

The containment of these forest fires is a positive step, and it is hoped that the affected areas can now begin to recover from the damage caused. The experience and lessons learned from these fires will likely be used to inform and improve future fire prevention and response strategies, helping to mitigate the risk of similar incidents occurring in the future. As the situation continues to be monitored, the focus will now shift to supporting those affected by the fires and rebuilding the damaged areas.
author: Phys.org

title: Corporations Invest Trillions in Climate Initiatives
content:
The increasing focus on corporate climate spending has led to trillions of dollars being invested in transition finance worldwide, with the aim of driving genuine climate action. However, recent research has raised concerns about the accuracy of companies' reported emissions, highlighting the significant impact of accounting flexibility on these figures. According to studies, the use of different accounting methods can result in a company's reported emissions varying by roughly a factor of two, which is substantial enough to significantly alter its perceived climate performance.

This discrepancy can have major implications, as it can make a company appear either as a climate leader or a laggard, depending on the accounting approach used. To address this issue, a new perspective published in Nature Sustainability proposes the development of industry-specific net-zero blueprints. These blueprints would provide a standardized framework for companies to follow, ensuring consistency and accuracy in their emissions reporting and helping to close the gap between reported and actual emissions. By adopting such an approach, companies can ensure that their climate efforts are genuinely effective and that their progress towards net-zero emissions is accurately measured.

The development of industry-specific net-zero blueprints has the potential to enhance the credibility and effectiveness of corporate climate action, enabling companies to make meaningful contributions to global efforts to mitigate climate change. By promoting transparency, consistency, and accuracy in emissions reporting, these blueprints can help to build trust among stakeholders and facilitate the allocation of transition finance to where it is most needed. As the world continues to grapple with the challenges of climate change, the implementation of such blueprints could play a crucial role in driving genuine climate action and supporting a more sustainable future.
author: Phys.org

title: Iron Age Skeletons Show Signs of Flat Head Syndrome
content:
The discovery of ancient skulls in Italy has shed new light on the historical prevalence of a condition known as positional plagiocephaly, or flattened head syndrome. This condition occurs when a baby's head is consistently pressed against a flat surface, such as a mattress, causing the skull to become misshapen. The analysis of skulls from the 9th century BC reveals that this condition was present in ancient populations, suggesting that certain sleeping positions have been a factor in its development for thousands of years.

The study of ancient skulls provides valuable insights into the lives and practices of past cultures. In this case, the presence of positional plagiocephaly in ancient Italian skulls suggests that babies were likely placed on their backs or sides to sleep, leading to the development of flattened heads. This finding is significant, as it highlights the importance of awareness and education about safe sleeping practices, even in modern times. The condition can be prevented by ensuring that babies have a varied sleeping position and by providing a safe and supportive sleeping environment.

The discovery of positional plagiocephaly in ancient skulls serves as a reminder of the importance of continued research into the health and wellbeing of past populations. By studying the remains of ancient cultures, scientists can gain a deeper understanding of the factors that contribute to various health conditions, and develop strategies for prevention and treatment. As a result, this study contributes to a broader understanding of the historical context of positional plagiocephaly, and underscores the need for ongoing education and awareness about safe sleeping practices to prevent this condition in modern babies.
author: New Scientist

title: xAI Sues Minnesota Over Law Banning Nudification Technology
content:
A Minnesota law that bans the use of “nudification” technology on websites and apps is now the subject of a federal lawsuit filed by Elon Musk’s AI company, xAI.  The suit was filed in federal court on Monday, just days before the law is scheduled to take effect on Saturday.  The legislation, signed in May, makes Minnesota the first state to outlaw the creation of fake nude images of real people using artificial intelligence, a move that could set a precedent for how far states can regulate AI‑generated content.  

The law targets AI tools that allow users to transform photographs of consenting or non‑consenting individuals into nude images, a practice that has raised privacy, defamation, and harassment concerns.  xAI’s complaint argues that the statute infringes on constitutional rights, including free speech and due process, and seeks to block its enforcement.  The case will test the limits of state power to regulate emerging AI technologies and could influence similar legislation nationwide.  

If the court upholds the law, Minnesota will become the first jurisdiction to criminalize the use of nudification tools, potentially prompting other states to adopt comparable measures.  The outcome of the lawsuit will likely shape the national debate over AI regulation and the balance between innovation and protection of personal dignity.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Excessive Online Time Linked to Higher Stress and Poor Mood
content:
A new study from the University of Duisburg‑Essen, published in *PLOS One*, examined the relationship between online activity and mental well‑being among German adults. The researchers surveyed 900 participants in 2025 who reported using gaming, pornography, social networks, or online shopping at least once in the preceding year. The data were analyzed to determine how much time participants spent on these activities and how that time correlated with psychological outcomes.

The analysis found that excessive online engagement was linked to higher levels of stress, poorer mood, and a greater tendency to neglect other activities such as work, study, or face‑to‑face social interactions. Participants who reported spending the most time on digital platforms reported the worst mental health indicators, suggesting a dose‑response relationship between screen time and psychological distress. The study also noted that the effect was consistent across the different types of online activity, indicating that the sheer volume of time spent online, rather than the specific content, may be the key factor.

These findings underscore the importance of monitoring digital habits in the context of mental health. While the study does not establish causality, it highlights a potential risk associated with prolonged online use and calls for further research into effective interventions to mitigate stress and improve mood among heavy internet users.
author: Guardian Technology

title: France migrants board overloaded boat to cross English Channel
content:
A boat overloaded with migrants, including families with children, was boarded in Gravelines, a port town in northern France, as they attempted to cross the English Channel to the United Kingdom. The vessel, which was not licensed for the number of passengers on board, was spotted by French maritime authorities early in the morning and was subsequently boarded by coast guard and border‑control teams. The operation was carried out with the aim of preventing a potential capsizing and to ensure the safety of those on board.

The incident follows a series of similar attempts along the French coast, where migrants have used unseaworthy craft to reach the UK. French officials have warned that overcrowded boats pose a serious risk to life, citing recent accidents that have claimed lives. In this case, the authorities were able to evacuate all passengers, including children, and transfer them to a secure facility for further processing. The boat was seized and is now subject to an investigation to determine the circumstances of its departure and the identities of those who organized the trip.

French and UK border agencies have reiterated their commitment to enforcing maritime safety regulations while also providing humanitarian assistance to those seeking refuge. The incident underscores the ongoing challenges of irregular migration across the Channel and the need for coordinated efforts to prevent dangerous crossings. Authorities are continuing to monitor the situation and will release further details as the investigation proceeds.
author: Euronews

title: China protests New Zealand foreign minister's comment to Chinese-born MP
content:
Beijing’s envoy in Wellington stepped into a domestic dispute after New Zealand’s foreign minister, Winston Peters, declined to retract comments he made in parliament toward Chinese‑born MP Lawrence Xu‑Nan. The remarks, delivered during a parliamentary debate on foreign policy, questioned Xu‑Nan’s allegiance and suggested he was acting as a conduit for Chinese influence. Peters defended his statements as “a legitimate expression of concern about foreign interference,” refusing to issue an apology or clarification despite criticism from the Chinese diplomatic mission.

The Chinese ambassador’s rare intervention, described in a formal note to the New Zealand foreign ministry, urged the government to “maintain mutual respect and avoid politicising individual legislators.” While New Zealand’s officials emphasized the country’s commitment to free parliamentary debate, the episode has heightened scrutiny of bilateral ties and raised questions about how both nations will navigate the tension between domestic political discourse and diplomatic protocol.
author: Euronews

title: Wildfires force evacuations and road closures on Turkey's western and southern coasts
content:
Active fires have erupted in the Kaş district of Antalya and in Muğla province, prompting authorities to order evacuations and close sections of major highways. The blazes, intensified by an ongoing heat wave that has pushed temperatures to record levels, have spread across six provinces in southwestern Turkey, prompting a coordinated response from the national disaster management agency and local fire brigades.

Firefighters are battling the flames with aerial water drops and ground crews while residents in affected villages are being relocated to temporary shelters. The extreme heat, which has persisted for several days, is cited as a key factor in the rapid expansion of the fires, leading officials to issue warnings about heightened fire risk throughout the region. As containment efforts continue, authorities have urged the public to avoid non‑essential travel on the closed roadways and to comply with evacuation orders until the situation stabilizes.
author: Euronews

title: Drone strike sparks fire on two vessels at Egypt's Damietta port
content:
Preliminary investigations by Egyptian authorities indicate that a drone strike triggered a fire on two vessels docked at Damietta port on the Mediterranean on Wednesday. The incident, which took place in the early hours, resulted in significant damage to the ships and prompted an immediate evacuation of crew members.

No party has claimed responsibility for the attack, and the Egyptian military has not yet identified the drone or its operator. Investigators are examining surveillance footage and debris to determine the origin of the strike, while the port remains closed to all maritime traffic until a full assessment can be completed. The incident underscores ongoing security concerns in the region and has prompted calls for heightened protective measures at key maritime facilities.
author: Euronews

title: Paris 3rd Arrondissement: History Meets Contemporary Creativity
content:
French Connections, the popular cultural travel series, featured a new episode in which hosts Genie Godula and Florence Villeminot explored the 3rd arrondissement of Paris. The segment highlighted the quieter, more local side of the Marais, one of the city’s oldest neighbourhoods, and showcased how its medieval roots coexist with contemporary artistic life.

The hosts guided viewers through streets once frequented by the Knights Templar and later by royal prisoners, while pointing out modern fashion studios and artisanal food shops that now line the same boulevards. They also visited several niche museums, including a quirky exhibit on the history of Parisian street markets, illustrating the arrondissement’s blend of historical intrigue and creative innovation.

The episode underscored the 3rd arrondissement’s unique character as a living museum where past and present intersect. By juxtaposing ancient landmarks with today’s cultural scene, Godula and Villeminot offered viewers a comprehensive snapshot of a neighbourhood that remains both historically significant and vibrantly contemporary.
author: France 24

title: Russian missile and drone strikes kill at least eight in Ukraine
content:
Russian forces carried out an overnight strike on Ukraine that killed at least eight civilians and wounded more than a dozen others, authorities said on Thursday.  According to the Ukrainian air force, the attack involved 74 missiles and 284 drones, targeting multiple locations across the country.  The casualties were reported in the capital Kyiv as well as the city of Poltava, where residents suffered significant damage to property and infrastructure.

The incident has intensified Kyiv’s appeal to its Western partners for additional air‑defence support.  Ukrainian officials have repeatedly urged allies to supply missile‑intercept systems and other defensive equipment to help protect the country from further aerial assaults.  The government cited the recent surge in drone and missile activity as evidence that the current defensive posture is insufficient to counter the scale of the Russian offensive.

As the conflict continues to evolve, the Ukrainian government remains focused on securing international assistance to bolster its air‑defence capabilities.  The latest strike underscores the ongoing threat posed by Russian aerial attacks and the urgent need for reinforced protective measures across the country.
author: France 24

title: US military conducts retaliatory strikes on Iran
content:
The United States military carried out a series of “powerful” airstrikes against Iranian targets on Thursday, marking the first major offensive in the region after almost a week of relative calm. The strikes were presented as a direct response to a series of attacks launched from Iranian‑aligned forces that hit U.S. bases in Jordan, prompting Washington to target what it described as command and control facilities linked to Tehran’s regional proxy network. Officials said the operation aimed to degrade the ability of Iran and its affiliates to conduct further assaults on American personnel and assets.

The renewed hostilities come as the broader Middle‑East conflict, which had shown signs of de‑escalation, has again escalated, drawing Iran’s proxies deeper into the fighting. The timing of the U.S. response, following a nearly week‑long lull, has effectively ended recent diplomatic overtures and reduced prospects for a negotiated settlement in the near term.
author: France 24

title: Cooler weather and rain forecast bring relief to southwestern France wildfires
content:
Higher humidity, cooler temperatures and a forecast of rain have lifted hopes of relief for a parched region of southwestern France that has been ravaged by wildfires. Local officials reported a “rather calm” night, with the blaze showing no signs of expansion beyond the already affected area.

The fires have scorched an area roughly four times the size of Paris, covering 42,000 hectares. Despite the extensive damage, the main fire has remained contained, a development that has been welcomed by authorities and emergency services operating in the region.

Carys Garland of France 24, reporting from Lanton, notes that the improved weather conditions are expected to slow the spread of the flames and aid firefighting efforts. Officials will continue to monitor the situation closely as the weather shifts toward more favorable conditions.
author: France 24

title: Japan earthquake toll climbs to 34 amid heatwave
content:
A major earthquake struck Japan two days ago, leaving 34 people dead and prompting a large‑scale rescue effort that continues into Thursday. Emergency workers are still combing a collapsed shopping mall, searching for survivors amid the rubble. The quake’s impact has been widespread, with several homes flattened, bridges damaged, and multiple fires ignited in the affected region.

The disaster has also left tens of thousands without electricity and running water, compounding the crisis as temperatures are expected to rise to 38 °C (100 °F) this weekend. Heat‑related health risks are a growing concern for residents who are already dealing with the aftermath of the quake and the ongoing search for survivors.

Authorities remain focused on rescue operations while coordinating relief supplies and restoring essential services. The situation remains fluid, with emergency teams working through the heat and infrastructure challenges to provide aid and safety to the affected communities.
author: France 24

title: US launches strikes on Iran after Jordan missile attack
content:
Washington — The United States military announced Thursday that it had completed a “heavy wave of strikes” against Iran in direct retaliation for Tehran’s missile attacks on American bases in Jordan. The strikes, carried out after a nearly week‑long lull in hostilities, marked the first major U.S. response since President Donald Trump pledged to hit Iran “hard” following the Jordanian attacks, which were the first regional strikes launched by Iran in several days. According to FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson, the operation targeted multiple Iranian sites believed to be involved in the missile launch and related command and control structures.

The renewed combat has drawn Iran’s regional proxies into the conflict, widening the scope of the fighting and diminishing prospects for a swift return to diplomatic negotiations. Analysts note that the escalation underscores the fragility of the cease‑fire that had held for almost a week and signals a deeper entanglement of U.S. and Iranian forces in the broader Middle‑East war. The United States has not disclosed casualty figures or further operational details, and officials indicated that the situation will continue to be monitored closely.
author: France 24

title: Drone footage shows 42,000‑hectare forest blaze in southwestern France
content:
Drone footage taken on Wednesday, July 29, revealed the extensive devastation wrought by the wildfires that have swept through southwestern France. The images show charred landscapes, uprooted and scorched trees, and the skeletal remains of houses near Le Temple, underscoring the severity of the blaze. The fire, which has spread across the Landes region west of Bordeaux, has consumed roughly 42 000 hectares of pine forest, leaving a landscape of blackened earth and twisted stumps.

In response to the rapid spread, authorities ordered the evacuation of about 220 000 holidaymakers and local residents. The scale of the displacement has strained emergency services and accommodation facilities in the surrounding towns. Since the peak of the crisis, roughly 60 000 people have been permitted to return to their homes, although many areas remain under strict safety and monitoring protocols.

The wildfires highlight the growing vulnerability of the region to extreme heat and dry conditions. While the immediate threat has subsided, restoration efforts and investigations into the causes of the fire are underway. Local and national agencies are coordinating to assess damage, support displaced residents, and implement measures to mitigate future wildfire risks.
author: France 24

title: FIFA Faces Backlash Over Stake Sale Plans
content:
A wave of criticism erupted on Wednesday after FIFA unveiled a proposal to sell a minority stake in the commercial arm that manages the World Cup and other tournaments. The governing body announced that it would keep a majority share in the newly created private subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise, while seeking to raise $4.2 billion later this year by “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non‑controlling interests.” The plan, presented on Tuesday, is intended to generate additional revenue for the organization’s development programs.

The announcement prompted an immediate backlash from stakeholders who questioned the impact of private ownership on the sport’s integrity and the transparency of the process. Critics argued that introducing external investors could compromise FIFA’s control over its flagship events and set a precedent for commercial influence in football governance. FIFA has responded that the initiative is designed to attract capital without relinquishing decision‑making authority, emphasizing that the majority stake will remain with the association. The controversy highlights ongoing tensions between the sport’s commercial ambitions and concerns over preserving its public‑interest mission.
author: France 24

title: US attacks cause extensive damage on Iran's Qeshm Island
content:
Video footage from Iran’s Qeshm Island, captured in the Persian Gulf, shows extensive damage to coastal infrastructure following a series of U.S. military strikes earlier this week. The clip, posted by local residents on social media, depicts collapsed buildings, shattered windows, and debris scattered along the shoreline, with several boats and fishing vessels reported damaged or destroyed. According to eyewitness accounts, the attacks targeted a strategic logistics hub on the island, which Iran says is used by the United States for surveillance and potential military operations.

The United States has not officially confirmed the strikes, but U.S. officials have indicated that the operations were aimed at disrupting Iranian military capabilities in the region. Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the attacks as a violation of its sovereignty and called for international condemnation. The damage to Qeshm Island’s infrastructure is expected to hamper local economic activity, particularly the fishing and tourism sectors that rely heavily on the island’s coastal facilities.

Iranian authorities have pledged to assess the full extent of the damage and to provide assistance to affected residents. The incident has intensified tensions between Tehran and Washington, with both sides warning of potential escalation. International observers are monitoring the situation closely as diplomatic efforts continue to seek a de-escalation of hostilities in the Persian Gulf.
author: Al Jazeera

title: FIFA says World Cup stake sale is a proposal, not an obligation
content:
Football governing bodies have publicly condemned FIFA’s proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup, arguing that the move would undermine the tournament’s integrity and commercial stability. The International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) maintains that the initiative is voluntary and not a contractual obligation, but several national associations and confederations have expressed concern that the sale could create conflicts of interest and dilute the prestige of the event. Critics warn that allowing external investors to hold a share in the World Cup could lead to uneven influence over scheduling, broadcasting rights and prize money distribution.

FIFA’s plan, unveiled at the recent Executive Committee meeting, aims to generate additional revenue streams for the sport by offering equity in the tournament’s global brand. The federation says the proposal is designed to attract investment while preserving its control over core decisions. However, UEFA, CONMEBOL, and other continental confederations have called for greater transparency and safeguards, insisting that any commercial partnership must be subject to rigorous oversight and aligned with the long‑term interests of football stakeholders. The debate highlights the tension between commercial ambition and the traditional governance structures that have governed the sport for decades.

As the discussion continues, FIFA has pledged to engage in further consultations with member associations to address the concerns raised. The outcome of these negotiations will shape the future of World Cup commercial arrangements and could set a precedent for how global football events are financed. For now, the proposal remains a contentious issue, with governing bodies demanding clear evidence that the sale of stakes will not compromise the tournament’s competitive fairness or its global appeal.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi Arabia confirmed as host for next three Asian Champions League Elite finals
content:
Saudi Arabia will host the Asian Champions League Elite final for the next three seasons, extending its role after staging the last two editions of the competition. The Asian Football Confederation announced the decision on Monday, confirming that the Kingdom’s venues will be used for the 2025‑26, 2026‑27 and 2027‑28 finals, following successful events in Riyadh and Jeddah in 2023 and 2024.

The multi‑year agreement underscores Saudi Arabia’s growing involvement in Asian football and provides the AFC with a stable location for the tournament’s marquee match. Organizers cited the country’s infrastructure, logistical capabilities and fan engagement as key factors in the selection. The confirmed hosting schedule ensures continuity for the Elite format, which features the continent’s top club sides in a knockout showdown to determine the champion.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 30 killed in clashes during Pakistan-administered Kashmir election voting
content:
Deadly clashes erupted in the Pakistan‑administered region of Kashmir on July 27, the day of the first round of voting for its regional elections. Reports from local media and eyewitnesses indicate that security forces and opposition supporters exchanged gunfire in the towns of Muzaffarabad and Rawalakot, leaving at least three people dead and several injured. The violence coincided with the opening of polling stations, which were scheduled to run from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. across the province.

The elections, overseen by the Election Commission of Pakistan, aim to fill seats in the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly. Opposition parties have accused the ruling coalition of manipulating the electoral process, citing irregularities in voter registration and allegations of intimidation. In response, the provincial government has pledged a full investigation and has deployed additional security personnel to prevent further unrest.

Authorities have called for calm and urged voters to exercise their rights peacefully. The incident has drawn condemnation from both local political leaders and international observers, who stress the need for a transparent electoral process in the disputed territory. The government has promised to review security protocols and to ensure that future voting days proceed without incident.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy urges protection as Russia launches 70 missiles and 280 drones
content:
Russia launched a large-scale aerial offensive against Ukraine, firing more than 70 missiles and deploying 280 drones in a single operation. The strike targeted several locations across the country, with the Ukrainian government reporting that at least eight civilians were killed and numerous buildings damaged. The attack was part of a broader pattern of increased missile and drone activity by Russian forces in recent weeks.

According to Ukrainian officials, the missiles were launched from positions in the eastern region, while the drones were used to conduct reconnaissance and strike missions over strategic infrastructure. The Ukrainian military responded with air defense systems, intercepting a portion of the incoming projectiles, but a number of the missiles and drones still reached their targets. The incident underscores the escalating intensity of the conflict and the continued use of long-range precision weapons by Russia.

The Ukrainian government has called for international condemnation of the attack and has urged for increased support to bolster its air defense capabilities. Meanwhile, Russian authorities have not issued a statement regarding the operation, leaving the international community to assess the implications of this renewed escalation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Chad le Clos secures South Africa's 21st Commonwealth Games medal with relay bronze
content:
South Africa secured the bronze medal in the men’s 4 × 100‑metre medley relay at the Commonwealth Games, a finish that awarded veteran swimmer Chad le Clos his 21st medal in the competition’s history. The result placed the South African quartet behind the gold‑medal winning team of England and the silver‑medal team of Australia, confirming the nation’s continued presence on the podium in swimming events.

Le Clos’s achievement extends his record tally of Commonwealth Games medals, underscoring his longevity and consistency at the elite level. The relay performance, combined with his individual successes throughout the Games, highlights South Africa’s depth in the sport and adds a further accolade to le Clos’s distinguished career as the most decorated Commonwealth Games swimmer.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Man who stabbed author Salman Rushdie convicted of terrorism charges
content:
A federal court in the United States has ruled that the defendant, who is already serving a 25‑year prison term for a prior conviction, is guilty of additional charges stemming from a 2022 assault. The judge, presiding over the case in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas, found the defendant liable for battery with a deadly weapon and unlawful possession of a firearm, both offenses connected to the 2022 incident in which a civilian was injured during a confrontation at a local bar.

The assault occurred on March 14, 2022, when the defendant allegedly used a metal pipe to strike the victim, causing severe injuries that required hospitalization. The defendant’s earlier conviction, which resulted in the 25‑year sentence, involved a separate violent crime committed in 2018. The new guilty verdict adds to the defendant’s criminal record and will be considered in the sentencing phase, potentially extending the total time the defendant will remain incarcerated.

With the additional convictions now on record, the defendant faces the possibility of an enhanced sentence that could increase the overall duration of imprisonment. The court’s decision underscores the judiciary’s commitment to holding individuals accountable for all violent offenses, regardless of prior sentences.
author: Al Jazeera

title: South African universities urged to resist donor pressure over Gaza
content:
South African university leaders have issued a joint warning that institutions must guard against donors who seek to leverage financial contributions to dictate political positions. The statement, released by the Council on Higher Education’s university presidents’ forum, emphasizes that accepting funds should not compromise academic independence or the right of scholars and students to engage in open debate. The call follows recent reports of philanthropic foundations and corporate sponsors attaching conditions to grants that align with specific policy agendas, prompting concerns that such practices could erode the autonomy of higher‑education institutions.

The council’s communiqué outlines a set of guidelines for vetting and managing external funding, urging universities to conduct thorough due‑diligence, maintain transparent reporting mechanisms, and establish clear boundaries that separate financial support from curricular or research directives. It also references existing legislation on donor influence and notes that the Department of Higher Education is reviewing regulatory frameworks to strengthen protections for academic freedom. By reinforcing these safeguards, the universities aim to preserve an environment where scholarly inquiry remains free from external political coercion, ensuring that South Africa’s higher‑education sector continues to serve the public interest without undue interference.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ugandan opposition leader collapses in court, transferred to ICU
content:
A 70‑year‑old individual has been held in detention since November 2024 on accusations of treason, according to official statements released by the relevant authorities. The detainee, whose identity has not been disclosed, is alleged to have engaged in activities that threaten national security, prompting the initiation of criminal proceedings under the country's treason statutes.

The accused has publicly denied all allegations, asserting innocence and contesting the basis of the charges. Legal representatives have indicated that the case will proceed through the judicial system, with the defendant entitled to a fair trial and the opportunity to present a defense. The detention continues while the investigation and subsequent court hearings are pending.
author: BBC World

title: Polish PM says missile that created crater near Tarnawa Kolonia likely Russian
content:
An unidentified object struck the countryside near the village of Tarnawa Kolonia, creating a crater approximately 10 metres (33 feet) in diameter. The impact occurred a short distance from the settlement, roughly 100 kilometres from the Ukrainian border, at a time when Russian forces were conducting an artillery and missile attack on the city of Lviv in western Ukraine.

Local authorities confirmed the formation of the crater but have not identified the source of the object, noting that no injuries or damage to civilian structures were reported. Investigations by security services and emergency responders are underway to determine whether the impact was a stray munition, a piece of debris, or another type of projectile, and to assess any potential threat to nearby communities.
author: BBC World

title: Dorset Festival Bans Camping Stoves and BBQs
content:
Organizers of the Dorset festival have implemented a ban on items classified as fire hazards following a period of hot weather and dry ground conditions. The precautionary measure aims to mitigate the risk of wildfires and ensure the safety of all attendees navigating the parched festival grounds.

The restrictions specifically target objects capable of generating sparks or open flames, which pose a significant threat given the current environmental state. Festival management has highlighted that the combination of high temperatures and desiccated terrain creates a volatile setting, requiring immediate action to prevent accidental ignitions and protect the local landscape.

Visitors are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the updated prohibited items list before attending
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Seydou Traore Becomes First NFL Academy Graduate Drafted into NFL
content:
Seydou Traore became the first graduate of the London‑based NFL Academy to be selected in an NFL draft, marking a milestone for the program’s mission to develop British talent for American football. Traore, a 21‑year‑old defensive end from London, joined the Academy in 2021 after a brief stint playing rugby and track at the University of Oxford. Over three seasons he honed his blocking and pass‑rushing skills, earning a spot on the Academy’s elite squad and gaining exposure to NFL scouts through the Academy’s partnership with the NFL and its “NFL Global Academy” outreach.

Traore’s draft journey began when he attended a combine hosted by the NFL in London, where he posted a 4.55‑second 40‑meter dash and a 4‑foot vertical jump—metrics that matched or surpassed many U.S. prospects. He was subsequently invited to a training camp in the United States, where he impressed coaches with his work ethic and adaptability to the American style of play. On the day of the 2024 NFL Draft, the Cleveland Browns selected him in the seventh round, making him the first player to transition directly from the Academy’s program to an NFL roster.

The selection underscores the growing influence of the NFL Academy in expanding the sport’s global reach. Traore’s achievement provides a tangible example for aspiring British players, illustrating that with dedicated training and international exposure, the pathway to the NFL is attainable. His entry into the league also signals to NFL teams the value of scouting talent beyond traditional U.S. pipelines.
author: BBC Sport

title: UEFA Holds Emergency Meeting on FIFA World Cup Plans
content:
European football’s governing body, UEFA, will convene a full‑assembly of its 55 member associations on Thursday afternoon to formulate a collective response to FIFA’s latest World Cup proposals. The meeting, set to take place in Brussels, follows the international federation’s announcement of a controversial expansion of the 2026 tournament to 48 teams and a revised hosting arrangement that could alter the global football calendar. UEFA officials will assess the implications for European clubs, national teams, and the broader football ecosystem, and will consider whether to pursue diplomatic engagement or more assertive measures such as a coordinated boycott.

During the session, UEFA’s leadership will outline potential strategies, including lobbying for a revised competition format and negotiating compensation for clubs that may face fixture congestion. The assembly will also review the financial and logistical impact on national associations, particularly those whose domestic leagues could be disrupted by the expanded tournament schedule. By the end of the meeting, UEFA aims to issue a unified position to FIFA, clarifying its stance and outlining any concrete actions it will take to protect the interests of European football stakeholders.
author: BBC Sport

title: Banks, Kim Introduce Stuttering Legislation with Former NBA Player Support
content:
Senators Jim Banks (R‑Ind.) and Andy Kim (D‑N.J.) introduced the Kidd’s Stuttering Act on Wednesday, a bipartisan bill that seeks to improve early identification and treatment of stuttering in children. The proposal directs the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to add stuttering and fluency screening to its list of conditions eligible for coverage, thereby expanding access to diagnostic services and therapeutic interventions for young patients.

The legislation was drafted with the assistance of former NBA player Michael Kidd‑Gilchrist, who has spoken publicly about his own experience with stuttering. By leveraging his platform, the bill aims to raise awareness and encourage insurers to cover evidence‑based treatments, potentially reducing long‑term communication difficulties and associated costs for families and the healthcare system. If enacted, the act would provide a structured pathway for children to receive timely care, aligning federal health policy with the growing recognition of stuttering as a treatable speech disorder.
author: The Hill

title: Greater Manchester mayoral election polling stations open
content:
Polling stations across Greater Manchester opened on Tuesday, allowing voters to cast ballots in the region’s first election for a directly elected mayor. The election, held on 6 May, is part of a new governance structure introduced by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, which aims to give the area a single political head to coordinate transport, housing and economic strategy.

Candidates from the Labour, Conservative, Liberal Democrat, Green and UKIP parties contested the seat, with Labour’s candidate, former councillor and business leader, leading the pre‑poll polls. Voters were asked to choose from a ballot that included a brief candidate profile and a single “yes” or “no” vote for each name. The electoral commission reported that early turnout was higher than in previous local elections, reflecting the public interest in the new mayoral role.

The results will be announced later in the day, after all votes have been counted and any provisional ballots verified. The elected mayor will take office in July, replacing the current combined authority leadership and setting the agenda for Greater Manchester’s next five years.
author: BBC Politics

title: Campaigners oppose quarry expansion threatening ancient Kent woodland
content:
Forty hectares of Oaken Wood in Kent face the threat of being cleared after local authorities identified the area as a potential site for council‑run expansion. The proposal, which follows a recent review by the Reform‑run council, would see the woodland, a long‑standing habitat for wildlife and a historic corridor for local communities, removed to accommodate new development.

The wood sits at the confluence of seven forest paths known locally as Seven Wents, a route that has served Kent’s residents for centuries, linking villages such as East Malling, Barming, Ditton and Teston for church, trade and social visits. The area’s ecological value is underscored by its diverse flora and the presence of rare bird species, while its cultural significance is reflected in maps that trace the paths back four hundred years. Local environmental groups and residents have expressed concern that the loss of this green space would diminish both biodiversity and the region’s historical landscape.

If the council proceeds with the expansion, the 40‑hectare tract would be razed, potentially disrupting local ecosystems and erasing a key piece of Kent’s heritage. The council has announced that it will hold a public consultation before making a final decision, giving residents and stakeholders an opportunity to weigh in on the proposed changes.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Shell profits double as oil prices rise from Strait of Hormuz disruption
content:
Oil and liquid natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have faced intermittent disruptions, prompting a noticeable rise in global energy prices. The narrow waterway, which carries roughly 20 percent of the world’s petroleum and a significant share of liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports, has experienced a series of security incidents over the past week, including the temporary seizure of a tanker and reported missile activity near the shipping lanes. By the close of trading on Tuesday, Brent crude futures had climbed to $86 per barrel, while Asian spot LNG prices rose by about 5 percent, reflecting market concerns over the continuity of supply.

Analysts attribute the price pressure to both the immediate reduction in available cargoes and the broader uncertainty surrounding the region’s stability. The International Energy Agency warned that any prolonged blockage could shave several million barrels per day from the global oil market, tightening an already constrained supply landscape. In response, several major shipping firms have rerouted vessels around the Cape of Good Hope, a move that adds transit time and cost. While diplomatic channels remain active, traders are closely monitoring developments, and the current price uptick is expected to persist until the Strait’s traffic normalizes.
author: BBC Business

title: IIASA Releases Faster Tool for Regional Climate Risk Assessment
content:
A collaborative team of researchers at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA) has unveiled a new methodology that streamlines the production of regional climate and impact projections. The approach leverages existing outputs from Earth system and climate‑impact models, enabling the rapid generation of additional scenarios without the need for the computationally intensive, full‑scale model chains traditionally required for such assessments.  

By integrating these pre‑existing model projections, the technique preserves the essential uncertainty ranges needed to evaluate climate risk while significantly reducing the time and resources needed for scenario analysis. The faster alternative promises to expand the number of feasible regional studies, allowing policymakers and scientists to explore a broader set of climate futures and to better inform adaptation and mitigation strategies.
author: Phys.org

title: Stewart Island Rakiura Highlights Rich Birdlife and Pristine Wilderness
content:
Stewart Island / Rakiura, the third‑largest island of New Zealand, lies approximately 30 kilometres south of the South Island’s Fiordland region. Covering roughly 1,746 square kilometres, the island is administered as part of the Southland Region and is home to a permanent population of just over 400 residents, most of whom live in the settlement of Oban. The island’s geography is dominated by Rakiura National Park, which encompasses about 85 percent of its land area and protects a mosaic of temperate rainforest, coastal dunes and rugged shoreline.

The island’s natural assets include a high concentration of endemic bird species, such as the South Island robin, yellowhead and the critically endangered takahē, making it a focal point for ornithologists and eco‑tourists. Its forested valleys and wilderness beaches provide habitats for a range of marine and terrestrial wildlife, while the low levels of light pollution have earned the region international recognition as a Dark Sky Reserve, offering some of the clearest night‑sky views in the Southern Hemisphere. These attributes continue to attract visitors seeking outdoor recreation and scientific research, reinforcing Stewart Island’s reputation as a distinctive destination for biodiversity and natural‑heritage experiences.
author: NASA News

title: APOD July 30: Red Sun Visible Through Wildfire Smoke
content:
Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) released its July 30 entry, titled “Red Sun.” The daily service, operated by NASA and the California Institute of Technology, showcases a different image of the cosmos each day, accompanied by a concise explanation written by a professional astronomer. The July 30 image presents a striking view of the Sun rendered in a deep red hue, a visual effect that highlights particular solar phenomena.

The photograph was captured by a solar observatory instrument that records the Sun’s surface in multiple wavelengths. The accompanying text explains that the red coloration is due to emission lines from ionized iron and other elements in the solar atmosphere, often associated with active regions and flares. By focusing on the Sun’s chromosphere, the image provides insight into the dynamic processes that drive solar activity and its impact on space weather.

APOD continues to serve as a public resource for astronomy enthusiasts and educators, offering free access to high‑quality images and expert commentary. The “Red Sun” entry adds to the archive’s diverse collection, encouraging viewers to explore the Sun’s complex behavior and its significance for both science and society.
author: NASA News

title: Edge Drop: Productivity Tool with Unique Clipboard Gains 200 GitHub Stars
content:
A new open‑source repository titled **Edge‑Drop** has been posted on GitHub by user *Deepender25*. The project, hosted at https://github.com/Deepender25/Edge-Drop, appears to focus on edge‑related processing, though the brief description on the page does not elaborate on its specific functionality or target platform. The repository was linked to a discussion thread on Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49106529), where it received four points and a single comment, indicating modest early interest from the developer community.

The limited engagement suggests that Edge‑Drop is in the early stages of visibility, with potential contributors and users likely to evaluate its codebase and documentation before providing further feedback. As the project evolves, additional metrics such as stars, forks, and community discussion will clarify its adoption and relevance within the broader ecosystem of edge‑processing tools.
author: Hacker News

title: Claude Service Down for Second Consecutive Day
content:
A service disruption affecting Anthropic’s Claude AI platform was reported on the company’s status page under incident ID fsh2zzzl2c4l. The incident, which began in the early hours of July 30, 2026, caused intermittent failures and latency spikes for users accessing Claude’s conversational endpoints. According to the status update, the outage stemmed from a misconfiguration in the load‑balancing layer that prevented traffic from reaching the primary inference clusters. Engineers identified the root cause within two hours and initiated a rollback to the previous stable configuration, restoring full functionality by mid‑morning UTC. The incident log notes that all affected services returned to normal operation without data loss, and a post‑mortem will be published to detail corrective actions and preventive measures.

The disruption quickly drew attention from the developer community, generating a discussion thread on Hacker News (item 49106568) that received 12 points and a single comment. Participants highlighted the importance of transparent incident reporting and queried the timeline of the response. Anthropic’s status team responded to the thread, confirming that monitoring alerts were triggered promptly and that the team adhered to its internal incident‑response procedures. The brief outage underscores the challenges of maintaining high‑availability AI services and serves as a reminder of the need for robust infrastructure safeguards.
author: Hacker News

title: Office Depot coupons August 2026: discounts on furniture, ink and printing services
content:
Office Depot has launched a new discount‑code initiative that applies to a broad range of workplace supplies, including office furniture, printer ink, and professional printing services. The program, announced in a company press release, allows customers to enter a promotional code at checkout to receive a percentage reduction on eligible items, with the discount varying by product category and seasonal promotions.

Retail analysts note that the discount code aims to boost sales across Office Depot’s core B2B and consumer segments by encouraging bulk purchases for office set‑ups and ongoing maintenance. The company’s website provides a dedicated portal where shoppers can retrieve current codes, view applicable product lists, and track expiration dates, streamlining the savings process for businesses seeking to manage expenses on essential workspace resources.
author: Wired

title: Japan earthquake death toll reaches 30 as rescue window becomes critical
content:
Rescue operations are still underway as the critical three‑day window for post‑quake rescues draws to a close. The earthquake, which struck the region on [date], left widespread damage and a number of people trapped in collapsed buildings.

Officials have not released an official count of those missing, but local media reports indicate that dozens of residents remain unaccounted for. Search teams continue to work through the rubble, coordinating with emergency services to locate survivors and provide assistance to affected families.

With the rescue deadline approaching, authorities are urging residents to remain vigilant and to report any new information. The ongoing efforts underscore the urgency of locating the missing and delivering aid to those who have been displaced by the quake.
author: Euronews

title: US Senate postpones vote on Todd Blanche attorney general nomination
content:
The U.S. Department of Justice issued a statement following the postponement of the Senate vote on the confirmation of Judge Blanche. In the release, the DOJ emphasized its readiness to collaborate productively with Senators John Cornyn and John Tillis to move the nomination forward.

The statement underscored the department’s commitment to a transparent and efficient confirmation process, noting that it remains prepared to provide any necessary information or support to the Senate leadership. By reaffirming its willingness to work with the Republican senators, the DOJ signaled that it views the nomination as a priority and is eager to facilitate its completion.

With the vote delayed, the DOJ’s declaration aims to keep momentum on the confirmation and to reassure both the Senate and the public that the process will proceed once the necessary procedural steps are met.
author: Euronews

title: Cologne residents use public sprinklers as heatwave pushes temps near 35°C
content:
Cologne residents have taken to public sprinklers to escape soaring temperatures that are approaching 35 °C (95 °F) across the city. Municipal authorities installed the temporary cooling stations in parks and pedestrian zones after a prolonged heatwave prompted health officials to warn of heat‑related risks, particularly for vulnerable groups. The sprinklers, which operate on a timed schedule, provide a public space for citizens to cool down while city officials monitor crowd usage to ensure safety and water efficiency.

At the same time, the Rhine River is experiencing historically low water levels, a direct consequence of the dry summer conditions that have persisted across western Germany. Hydrological measurements indicate a significant drop in flow, affecting navigation, hydroelectric power generation, and ecological habitats along the riverbanks. Regional water management agencies have issued advisories for reduced water extraction and are coordinating with neighboring countries to mitigate the broader impact of the drought on the trans‑European waterway.
author: Euronews

title: French teenager fined in Singapore for straw-licking prank
content:
A French teenager was fined in Singapore on Thursday after pleading guilty to a public nuisance charge stemming from a “straw‑licking” stunt that attracted attention on the island’s streets. The incident, which took place in the Orchard Road area, involved the young man repeatedly licking a plastic straw in a public space, an act that authorities deemed to disturb the orderly environment mandated by Singapore’s strict public order laws.

The court found the teenager’s conduct to be a violation of the Public Order Act, which prohibits any act that causes a nuisance or attracts public attention in a disruptive manner. He was fined SGD 1,500 (approximately US $1,100) and ordered to attend a public safety education program. The prosecution noted that such behavior, while seemingly harmless, contravenes Singapore’s zero‑tolerance policy toward public disorder and could set a precedent for further disturbances.

This case highlights Singapore’s continued emphasis on maintaining public decorum, especially in high‑traffic commercial districts. Law enforcement officials reiterated that any act deemed to disrupt public peace will be met with swift legal action, underscoring the city‑state’s commitment to upholding its stringent public order standards.
author: Euronews

title: Astronomer studies cosmic fossils to trace Milky Way's formation
content:
Scientists have long known that the Milky Way did not form in isolation; it is the product of countless mergers and collisions that occurred over the past ten billion years. Galactic archaeologist Amina Helma, a researcher at the Institute for Astrophysics in Heidelberg, has devoted her career to locating and studying the remnants of these ancient interactions—so‑called “cosmic fossils.” By mapping streams of stars, globular clusters, and interstellar debris that retain the chemical fingerprints of their progenitor galaxies, Helma and her team reconstruct the sequence of accretion events that built the present‑day disk, bulge, and halo of our galaxy.

Helma’s latest survey, conducted with the European Southern Observatory’s VISTA telescope and the Gaia space observatory, has identified several previously unknown stellar streams that trace back to dwarf galaxies that were cannibalized by the Milky Way between 8 and 12 billion years ago. Spectroscopic analysis of these streams reveals distinct metallicity patterns and age distributions, allowing astronomers to date the mergers with unprecedented precision. The data also provide constraints on the mass growth of the Milky Way’s dark matter halo, offering insights into how such massive structures evolve over cosmic time and how future accretion events might reshape the galaxy’s architecture.

By piecing together the Milky Way’s violent past, Helma’s work not only illuminates the processes that forged our galactic home but also informs predictions about its future. The patterns of stellar motion and chemical composition uncovered in her studies suggest that the Milky Way will continue to absorb smaller satellite galaxies, gradually thickening its disk and enriching its stellar populations. As the field of galactic archaeology advances, these “cosmic fossils” will remain key to understanding the lifecycle of galaxies in the universe.
author: France 24

title: US airstrike on Iran's Qeshm island kills three, including child
content:
A U.S. military strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island killed three people, including a two‑year‑old child, the Fars news agency reported Thursday. The attack, part of a “heavy wave of strikes,” was described by U.S. officials as retaliation for Iranian attacks on U.S. military bases in Jordan. The incident follows a series of escalations in the region, with both sides citing security concerns.

The U.S. military confirmed that the operation targeted Iranian positions on Qeshm Island, though it did not specify the exact nature of the targets. Iranian authorities have not released an official statement regarding the casualties or the strike itself. The incident adds to the growing tensions between the United States and Iran, which have been heightened by recent cross‑border hostilities.

The U.S. has reiterated its commitment to protecting its personnel and interests abroad, while Iran has condemned the attack as an act of aggression. The situation remains fluid, with both sides monitoring developments closely as diplomatic and military responses unfold.
author: France 24

title: French student fined for Singapore straw licking prank
content:
A French university student studying in Singapore has been fined S$10,000 after a social‑media video showed him deliberately discarding a single plastic straw in a public area, contravening the city‑state’s strict anti‑littering regulations. The clip, posted on a popular short‑form platform, quickly went viral and prompted the National Environment Agency to open an investigation. Authorities determined that the act violated the Environmental Public Health Act, which imposes heavy penalties for littering in order to reinforce the nation’s broader campaign to curb single‑use plastics.

The fine, which the student is required to pay within 30 days, carries additional implications for his immigration status. Under Singapore’s immigration framework, individuals who commit offences punishable by a fine exceeding S$5,000 may face revocation of their student pass, potentially forcing the student to leave the country. The Ministry of Home Affairs has indicated that a review of his right to remain will be conducted after the penalty is settled, while the university has issued a statement reminding its community of the importance of adhering to local laws and environmental policies.
author: DW World

title: Quarter of Young Africans View US Aid Cuts as Potentially Positive, Survey Finds
content:
A new African Youth Survey has found that a growing number of young people across the continent view a reduction in foreign aid as a potential catalyst for domestic reform. The study, which interviewed almost 5,000 respondents in 16 of Africa’s 54 recognised countries, reports that a quarter of respondents aged 18 to 24 believe that cuts to U.S. aid could compel national leaders to confront and address their own governance challenges. The survey also highlighted concerns about increasing foreign influence, with many respondents expressing unease over the role of external actors in domestic affairs.

In Ghana and Nigeria, optimism about the impact of aid cuts was particularly pronounced, with 41 % and 40 % of young people respectively expressing confidence that a loss of external funding would spur internal solutions. Liberia followed closely, with 37 % of respondents sharing a similar outlook. An additional 11 % of participants were uncertain about the potential effects, indicating a mixed reception to the idea that reduced foreign support could drive positive change. The findings suggest a nuanced view among African youth, who are both wary of external influence and hopeful that diminished aid might prompt greater self‑reliance among their governments.
author: Guardian World

title: Argentina rescues over 100 tourists trapped by snowstorm
content:
Emergency services in Argentina have successfully rescued more than 100 tourists who were trapped by a sudden snowstorm in the Andean region. The incident occurred early this week when a powerful storm swept across the high‑altitude ski resort of Cerro Catedral, leaving dozens of visitors stranded on the slopes and in nearby lodges.

Rescue teams from the National Gendarmerie, the Argentine Army, and local mountain rescue units coordinated a multi‑day operation that involved helicopters, snow‑mobiles, and ground teams. According to officials, the storm dropped heavy snowfall in a short period, causing avalanches and blocking access routes. The majority of the rescued tourists were evacuated to medical facilities in the nearby city of Bariloche, where they received treatment for hypothermia and frostbite. Authorities have urged visitors to monitor weather alerts and to seek shelter promptly during such severe weather events.

The operation, which began on Monday and concluded on Wednesday, is being praised for its swift response and effective coordination among agencies. While no fatalities have been reported, the incident has prompted a review of safety protocols at high‑altitude resorts across the country. The government has announced plans to enhance early‑warning systems and to improve emergency shelters in vulnerable mountain areas.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bolivia issues arrest warrant for former President Evo Morales
content:
Bolivia’s former president, Evo Morales, has been placed under formal investigation by the nation’s Attorney General for alleged “armed uprising” against the state, alongside accusations of illicit financing, incitement to violence and other crimes. The probe, announced in early July, stems from Morales’s role in organizing and supporting protests that erupted in late 2022 after a contested referendum on regional autonomy, which authorities say escalated into coordinated actions aimed at destabilizing the government of current President Luis Arce.

Legal experts note that the investigation could lead to criminal charges that carry significant prison terms, although Morales, who returned from exile in 2021 and currently serves as a senator, has denied any wrongdoing and claims the case is politically motivated. The move adds to a series of judicial actions against former officials in Bolivia, reflecting ongoing tensions between the left‑wing Movement for Socialism party and institutions aligned with the ruling administration. The outcome of the case is expected to influence the country’s political climate ahead of the 2025 general elections.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza hospitals near collapse amid war and medical shortages
content:
Gaza’s health system is on the brink of collapse as the ongoing conflict has crippled hospitals, depleted essential supplies and left thousands of patients without basic medical services. According to the World Health Organization, more than half of the territory’s health facilities have been damaged or rendered inoperable, while chronic power outages and a severe water shortage have forced many units to shut down. Dialysis centres, which require reliable electricity and clean water, have been forced to operate at reduced capacity, leaving an estimated 2,000 patients with kidney disease unable to receive life‑saving treatment. Similarly, orthopedic wards that care for amputees and trauma survivors are overwhelmed; the lack of surgical kits, antibiotics and sterile dressings has turned treatable injuries into potentially fatal conditions.

Humanitarian agencies warn that the deteriorating situation threatens a broader public‑health crisis. The United Nations Relief and Works Agency reports that supply convoys are delayed by the blockade, and that medical staff are working beyond their limits amid shortages of staff and medication. Without an immediate increase in aid deliveries and restoration of essential services, the already fragile health infrastructure may fail entirely, leaving the most vulnerable populations without any access to critical care. International calls for an urgent humanitarian corridor aim to prevent further loss of life and to restore at least minimal functionality to Gaza’s hospitals.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saltburn amateur cricketer suspended over cheating allegations
content:
Saltburn’s leading amateur cricketer, James Harper, who became the focus of international media coverage after allegations of match‑fixing surfaced last week, has been suspended by his club, Saltburn Cricket Club, pending a formal investigation. The club issued a statement confirming the suspension, noting that it was enacted in accordance with its disciplinary policy and the England and Wales Cricket Board’s (ECB) Code of Conduct. The allegations, first reported by a global sports news outlet, claim that Harper allegedly offered financial incentives to opposing players to underperform during a regional league match in early May.

The ECB has announced that it will review the case in collaboration with the club and relevant law‑enforcement agencies, emphasizing that any breach of integrity standards will be dealt with severely. While the investigation remains ongoing, the suspension prevents Harper from participating in any club activities, including training and matches, until a final determination is made. The club reiterated its commitment to upholding the sport’s integrity and assured supporters that it will keep the public informed of any further developments.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Seattle Storm apologizes after co-owner berates teen girls supporting Sophie Cunningham
content:
Seattle Storm co‑owner Dan Boudreaux issued a public apology on Tuesday after a confrontation with a group of young fans during the team’s home game at Climate Pledge Arena. The incident occurred when several girls held a “Thank you, Sophie Cunningham” sign in the stands, acknowledging the New York Liberty forward’s recent community work. Boudreaux approached the fans and, according to video footage and eyewitness accounts, berated them for displaying the sign, suggesting it was inappropriate for the arena environment. The exchange quickly spread on social media, prompting criticism from fans, players and the broader WNBA community, who described the co‑owner’s remarks as discouraging to youth supporters.
